questions.text: DeepMind released WaveNet, which generates raw audio waveforms, in which year?
questions.explanation: DeepMind released WaveNet in September 2016, showing that deep learning could model raw audio directly. 2018 is the tempting answer because Tacotron 2 arrived then, but WaveNet itself dates to 2016.

questions.text: Who published the first neural style transfer paper in 2015?
questions.explanation: Leon Gatys and colleagues released 'A Neural Algorithm of Artistic Style' on arXiv in 2015, applying a trained convolutional network to repaint photos in another image's style. Ian Goodfellow is the tempting answer as another famous generative-AI pioneer, but GANs are his, not style transfer.
answerAliases: A Neural Algorithm of Artistic Style

questions.text: Which open-source project launched in March 2023 kicked off the autonomous-agent craze?
questions.explanation: AutoGPT, released in March 2023, let a GPT-4 model loop over its own outputs and tool calls with no human in the loop, which is what started the agent gold rush. LangChain is the tempting answer as the most-used agent framework, but it is a library, not the project that sparked the craze.

questions.text: OpenAI announced GPT-4 in which month of 2023?
questions.explanation: OpenAI announced GPT-4 on March 14, 2023, and it powered the paid tier of ChatGPT from launch. January is the tempting answer because ChatGPT itself had just gone viral, but GPT-4 came two months later.

questions.text: Google announced Bard in which month of 2023?
questions.explanation: Google announced Bard on February 6, 2023, the week before Microsoft's Bing Chat event, as a direct response to ChatGPT. April is the tempting answer because that is when early access opened, but the announcement came in February.

questions.text: In which year did Meta release the first LLaMA model?
questions.explanation: Meta released LLaMA on February 24, 2023, initially to researchers under a non-commercial license. 2022 is the tempting answer because that was the ChatGPT shockwave year, but LLaMA came the following February.

questions.text: DeepMind's AlphaStar beat professional players at which game?
questions.explanation: AlphaStar defeated professional StarCraft II players in 2019 using a multi-agent reinforcement learning setup. Dota 2 is the tempting answer because OpenAI Five played that game the same year, but AlphaStar's game was StarCraft.

questions.text: Which DeepMind model learned to plan without knowing the rules of the game?
questions.explanation: MuZero, published in 2019, learned its own model of the environment and planned with it, mastering Go, chess, shogi and Atari without being given the rules. AlphaZero is the tempting answer because it also masters games from scratch, but it was given the rules.

questions.text: OpenAI Five competed in which esport?
questions.explanation: OpenAI Five played Dota 2 and beat the reigning world champions OG in 2019. StarCraft II is the tempting answer because AlphaStar played that the same year, but OpenAI Five's game was Dota.

questions.text: Which 2022 DeepMind study argued that models were undertrained relative to data?
questions.explanation: DeepMind's Chinchilla paper in March 2022 argued that for a given compute budget, smaller models trained on more data outperform larger ones trained on less, and it showed this against DeepMind's own Gopher. PaLM is the tempting answer as another big 2022 model, but it came from Google Research and was itself one of the giant models Chinchilla's argument implied were undertrained.

questions.text: Which series of models is OpenAI best known for developing?
options: The GPT series of large language models
The Claude series of large language models
The Gemini series of large language models
The Llama series of large language models
questions.answer: The GPT series of large language models
questions.explanation: GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer, and the name has been carried through the whole line since the original 2018 model. The other three series on this list belong to Anthropic, Google and Meta, which is a quick way to rule three options out and check the fourth.
answerAliases: generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) series of large language models

questions.text: Anthropic and OpenAI are both headquartered in the same American city. Which city?
questions.explanation: Both are public benefit corporations registered and based in San Francisco, and both were founded by people who had just left the same organisation. The overlap in people, funding and hiring is the single largest structural fact about the frontier lab industry.

questions.text: Which French AI company, founded in 2023 and based in Paris, is known for open weight language models?
questions.explanation: Mistral released the Mixtral mixture of experts model under an Apache licence, which was the first genuinely competitive open weight model from a European lab. The valuation above 14 billion dollars makes it the most valuable European AI company.

questions.text: Which Hangzhou based AI company develops open weight models and is owned and funded by a hedge fund?
questions.explanation: DeepSeek is funded by High-Flyer, which is unusual, since it means the research is not being driven by outside investors looking for a return. Their reasoning models made strong performance on math and code benchmarks at unusually low cost, and the models were released with open weights.
answerAliases: Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd.

questions.text: Which Seattle based non-profit research institute was founded in 2014 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen?
questions.explanation: Ai2, as it styles itself, was built to do open research rather than to ship products, and the distinction matters. The Allen Institute for Brain Science is a separate organisation in Seattle that studies neural tissue, and the two are easy to mix up because they share a name and a benefactor.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

questions.text: Which lab was founded in 2010, acquired by Google in 2014, and later merged with Google Brain in 2023?
questions.explanation: DeepMind was founded in London and became the company behind AlphaGo, AlphaFold and Gemini. Google paid a reported 400 million pounds for it, and the merge with Google Brain in April 2023 is what created the awkward situation of two research groups with the same name inside one company.

questions.text: Which Toronto based company focuses on large language models for regulated industries such as banking and healthcare?
questions.explanation: Aidan Gomez, Ivan Zhang and Nick Frosst founded Cohere in 2019, and Gomez was also the first author of the transformer paper that everything modern is built on. The pitch is deployment inside regulated companies rather than a consumer chatbot, which is a slower business with far fewer users.

questions.text: In which year did Google merge DeepMind with its Google Brain division to form Google DeepMind?
questions.explanation: Google had already bought DeepMind in 2014, and for nine years it and Google Brain ran as separate organisations with overlapping goals. The 2023 merge left one research lab with a duplicated name inside it, which is a fairly ordinary outcome of acquisitions and an unusually visible one here.

questions.text: Which lab develops the Claude family of AI models?
questions.explanation: Claude is the flagship product of Anthropic, the public benefit corporation founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members including Dario and Daniela Amodei with an explicit AI safety mission. OpenAI is the tempting wrong answer because the Amodeis came from there, but OpenAI builds the GPT series, not Claude.

questions.text: Which lab develops the Gemini family of AI models?
questions.explanation: Google DeepMind is responsible for the proprietary Gemini family alongside the open-weight Gemma models, after Google merged DeepMind with the Google Brain division in April 2023. OpenAI is the closest distractor since GPT and Gemini compete head to head, but GPT belongs to OpenAI.

questions.text: Which lab develops the Llama family of AI models?
questions.explanation: Meta AI is the research division behind the Llama models, which Meta released with open weights and built its Meta AI assistant on. Mistral AI is the natural confusion because the Paris lab also publishes open-weight models, but its family is Mistral and Mixtral, not Llama.

questions.text: Which former OpenAI chief scientist co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc.?
questions.explanation: Ilya Sutskever founded SSI with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy after leaving OpenAI in May 2024, with a mission focused on building safe superintelligence. Sam Altman is the closest distractor as the OpenAI CEO whose brief removal preceded Sutskever's exit, but Altman stayed and Sutskever left to start SSI.

questions.text: Which former OpenAI chief technology officer founded Thinking Machines Lab in 2025?
questions.explanation: Mira Murati, OpenAI's former chief technology officer, founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 as a San Francisco public benefit corporation. Ilya Sutskever is the tempting alternative because he also left OpenAI to found a lab, but his lab is SSI, founded a year earlier.

questions.text: What does World Labs, the startup founded by Fei-Fei Li, build?
options: AI accelerator chips for data centers
questions.explanation: World Labs came out of stealth in September 2024 with $230 million in funding to build large world models that perceive and interact with the 3D world, aimed at artists, designers and game studios. Protein folding is DeepMind's AlphaFold territory, while Li's bet is that spatial intelligence is the frontier after language.

questions.text: Which AI lab was created by Google LaMDA developers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas?
questions.explanation: Shazeer and De Freitas built LaMDA at Google, then left to found Character.ai, whose beta opened in September 2022 with customizable characters that users define and publish. Inflection AI is the closest distractor because it is also a chatbot lab, but its product was Pi and its founders came from DeepMind, not LaMDA.

questions.text: In August 2026, Google handed day-to-day leadership of Google DeepMind to a 13-year veteran of the lab, who took the new title of senior vice-president. Which veteran?
questions.explanation: Google's own memo announced that Koray Kavukcuoglu would step up as SVP of Google DeepMind, while Demis Hassabis gave up day-to-day operations to become chair of GDM and chief scientist of Alphabet. Kavukcuoglu had already been the lab's CTO and Google's chief AI architect. Oriol Vinyals is the tempting wrong answer because he was a DeepMind research VP at the time, but he left Google days later to co-found Discovery Loop.

source.label: Sundar Pichai and Demis Hassabis on the Google DeepMind leadership change

questions.text: In August 2026, Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le left Google together to found a new research lab. Which lab?
questions.explanation: Discovery Loop is a Palo Alto public benefit corporation whose stated goal is automating the propose-run-evaluate loop of scientific research, starting with machine learning itself. Google stayed in as a founding investor and cloud partner, so losing four researchers turned into an equity position. Ineffable Intelligence is the tempting wrong answer because it is the other ex-DeepMind lab that raised over a billion dollars, but David Silver founded that one months earlier.

questions.text: In the six days from June 18 to June 24, 2026, four senior Google DeepMind researchers said or were reported to be leaving for rival labs, and three of the four headed for the same company. Which company?
questions.explanation: John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold, announced first, and Gemini contributors Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel followed within days. Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer was the only one of the four who chose OpenAI, less than two years after Google paid billions to bring him back from Character.AI. Both OpenAI and Anthropic were close to going public, which is what made pre-IPO equity worth swapping a stable job for.

source.label: TechCrunch on the June 2026 Google departures

questions.text: In July 2026, Thinking Machines Lab co-founder Lilian Weng announced she was stepping down citing her health, then rejoined which lab two days later?
questions.explanation: Weng ran OpenAI's safety organisation before leaving in November 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines with Mira Murati, and she went back to lead a team supporting recursive self-improvement research. Murati stayed at her own lab, which is why the return looked awkward two days after the resignation note. Anthropic is the tempting wrong answer because it is Thinking Machines' most direct competitor.

questions.text: In August 2026, Nvidia's vice president of AI research left the company after eight years to found a Toronto startup building world models so robots can train inside simulation. Which researcher was that?
questions.explanation: Fidler ran Nvidia's Toronto spatial intelligence lab and was part of the team behind its Cosmos world model before announcing her departure. Her co-founders are Zan Gojcic, the former Nvidia research director in Zurich who is now CTO, and Huan Ling, her former doctoral student who is chief scientist. David Silver is the tempting wrong answer because he is the other ex-DeepMind founder with a billion-dollar lab, but his company is Ineffable Intelligence.

questions.text: In August 2026, the researcher who led Alibaba's Qwen model family founded a new AI lab in Shanghai. Which lab did he start?
questions.explanation: Junyang Lin left Alibaba in March 2026 with a post reading 'Bye my beloved Qwen', then named his new Shanghai lab after pragmatics, the study of meaning in context, which is roughly what an agent has to do. Zhipu AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is one of the best-known Chinese labs shipping open-weight models, but it has nothing to do with Lin. The Shanghai AI Laboratory is a real institute too, but a state-backed research body rather than a founder-led startup.

source.label: RuntimeWire on Junyang Lin's Pragmatik Labs

questions.text: In July 2026, Richard Sutton and his former student Khurram Javed left John Carmack's Keen Technologies to found a new lab in Toronto. What did they call it?
questions.explanation: Sutton, who shared the 2024 Turing Award for founding modern reinforcement learning, started Oak Lab to build agents that keep learning after deployment. His stated target is an agent with a trillion parameters that learns and plans in real time on about 20 watts, roughly human-brain power. Skyfall AI is the tempting wrong answer because it launched from Toronto in the same month, but it came from the Maluuba founders.

source.label: The Decoder on Oak Lab's launch

questions.text: In August 2026, a Princeton-rooted research lab for scientific computing came out of stealth with a $10.6 million round led by Dimension. Which of its three founders had previously co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project?
questions.explanation: Gorard is an applied mathematician who co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project with Stephen Wolfram and now runs Lanyon as CEO. His co-founders are Ammar Hakim, the computational physicist who is CTO, and James Juno, the plasma physicist. Ammar Hakim is the tempting wrong answer because he is the better-known senior scientist of the pair, but the Wolfram connection is Gorard's.

source.label: Physical AI News on Lanyon AI's founding team

questions.text: In August 2026, which US chipmaker unveiled its own long-horizon research lab, headquartered in Boise, Idaho?
questions.explanation: Micron Research Labs is a planned ten billion dollar research campus in Boise that will host hundreds of researchers working on memory and AI, with construction slated to begin in 2027. Nvidia is the tempting wrong answer because it is by far the largest AI chip company, but this is the American memory maker building for its own next decade alongside its two new Boise fabs.

source.label: Engineering News-Record on Micron Research Labs

questions.text: In July 2026, the LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and the Zynga founder Mark Pincus were reported to be backing a new research lab focused on computer-use models. Which lab?
questions.explanation: Prentis launched in April 2026 with serial entrepreneur Ritankar Das as CEO and trains models inside real office workflows rather than on web-scale text. Manas AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is Hoffman's own drug-discovery startup, which he went into founder mode on after leaving Microsoft's board. Inflection AI is the other lab he co-founded, back in 2022.

questions.text: Sakana AI, the Tokyo lab co-founded by Transformer paper co-author Llion Jones, takes its name from the Japanese word for what?
questions.explanation: Sakana AI's name is simply the Japanese word for fish, chosen by founders David Ha, Llion Jones and Ren Ito in 2023. Crane and blossom are the classic Japanese symbols a Tokyo lab might have picked for its brand, but the actual namesake is the fish.

questions.text: In April 2016, OpenAI released a public beta of which platform for developing and comparing reinforcement-learning algorithms?
questions.explanation: OpenAI Gym was the April 2016 public beta, a toolkit of environments and benchmarks that became the standard interface for reinforcement-learning research. Universe is the trap because OpenAI did ship that games platform too, but it arrived in December 2016, and Stable Baselines and RLlib are libraries built on top of the Gym ecosystem rather than OpenAI's own beta.

questions.text: Baidu's chatbot, built on its ERNIE models and launched to the public in 2023, was originally released under which Chinese name?
questions.explanation: Ernie Bot launched as Wenxin Yiyan (文心一言), which translates roughly as 'a word from the heart', and Baidu later shortened the name to Wenxiaoyan in September 2024. Tongyi Qianwen is the trap because that is the Chinese name of Alibaba's Qwen family, and Hunyuan belongs to Tencent.

questions.text: AI21 Labs, the Israeli maker of the Jurassic language models, was founded in which city in 2017?
questions.explanation: Amnon Shashua, Yoav Shoham and Ori Goshen founded AI21 Labs in Tel Aviv in November 2017 and later opened a US office while keeping the Israeli base. Jerusalem is the tempting miss because Shashua is a Hebrew University professor, but the company itself is Tel Aviv's.

questions.text: Which Beijing lab's Kimi assistant became famous for very long context windows?
questions.explanation: Moonshot AI, founded in 2023, marketed Kimi on context windows reaching into the hundreds of thousands of tokens when rivals offered far less. Zhipu AI is the natural confusion because it is another Beijing lab shipping open-weight models, but its family is GLM, not Kimi. Founder Yang Zhilin came from Tsinghua by way of CMU.

questions.text: Which lab, spun out of Tsinghua University, develops the GLM model family starting with ChatGLM?
questions.explanation: Zhipu grew out of Tsinghua's knowledge-engineering group and released ChatGLM as one of China's first strong open bilingual models. Moonshot AI is the tempting answer as the other famous Beijing open-weight lab, but Kimi is theirs and GLM is Zhipu's. The Wikipedia article lives under the company's newer name, Z.ai.

questions.text: The Allen Institute for AI, the open-model nonprofit abbreviated Ai2, is headquartered in which US city?
questions.explanation: Paul Allen founded the institute in 2014 and it has been based in Seattle ever since, later adding an office in Tel Aviv. San Francisco is the tempting answer because that is where most AI labs cluster, but Ai2 stayed in Allen's home city of Seattle.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

questions.text: Which company's enterprise model family is called Command, including Command R?
questions.explanation: Cohere, co-founded by transformer paper co-author Aidan Gomez, sells the Command family for retrieval-augmented enterprise work rather than running a consumer chatbot. Mistral AI is the tempting answer as the other open-weight enterprise lab, but its family is Mistral and Mixtral. Command R was built for grounding answers in company documents.

questions.text: Which pair of siblings co-founded Anthropic in 2021 after leaving OpenAI?
questions.explanation: Dario and Daniela Amodei left OpenAI in 2020 over safety disagreements and founded Anthropic as a public benefit corporation the next January. Altman and Brockman are the tempting answer because they stayed behind to run OpenAI, which is exactly the split that defines the frontier-lab rivalry. Claude is named for Claude Shannon, not for either founder.

questions.text: DeepSeek, the company behind the DeepSeek-R1 model, became an independent business in which month and year?
questions.explanation: High-Flyer, the quantitative hedge fund, announced an AGI research lab in April 2023 and spun it off as the independent company DeepSeek on 17 July 2023. April 2023 is the trap because that is when the lab was announced inside High-Flyer, and January 2025 is when the R1 model arrived, not the company.

questions.text: In which year did Elon Musk found xAI, the lab behind Grok?
questions.explanation: Musk announced xAI in July 2023, five years after leaving OpenAI's board, and released Grok months later. 2022 is the tempting answer because that was the ChatGPT shockwave year, but xAI came the summer after. Grok takes its name from Heinlein's Stranger in a Strange Land.

questions.text: Which lab's co-founder Mustafa Suleyman left in 2024 to run Microsoft AI, taking most of the staff with him?
questions.explanation: Suleyman co-founded Inflection in 2022 after leaving DeepMind, then Microsoft hired him along with most of the team in what everyone called an acquihire. Character.ai is the tempting answer because Google did a similar reverse-acquihire of its founders months later, but Suleyman's lab was Inflection. Its chatbot Pi played the friendly companion, not the search box.

questions.text: Which AI search lab was founded in 2022 by former OpenAI researcher Aravind Srinivas?
questions.explanation: Srinivas started Perplexity to answer questions with cited sources instead of ten blue links, and it became the defining AI search product. You.com is the tempting answer because it also wraps search in AI answers, but it was founded earlier by Richard Socher. Srinivas previously worked on transformers at OpenAI and Google.

questions.text: Which company was founded in 2016 by Clement Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf?
questions.explanation: The trio started Hugging Face as a chatbot app, then pivoted to the Transformers library and model hub that now hosts millions of models. Weights and Biases is the tempting answer as another beloved ML tooling company, but it does experiment tracking, not model hosting. The name and logo come from the hugging-face emoji.

questions.text: Which Beijing lab did investor and former Google China chief Kai-Fu Lee found in 2023?
questions.explanation: Lee launched 01.AI in March 2023 and reached unicorn valuation within months on the strength of his name alone. Moonshot AI is the tempting answer as the other famous 2023 Beijing lab, but that was Yang Zhilin's, not Lee's. Lee previously ran Google China and wrote the book AI Superpowers.

questions.text: DeepSeek and Alibaba are both headquartered in which Chinese city?
questions.explanation: Both the hedge-fund-backed DeepSeek and the e-commerce giant Alibaba sit in Hangzhou, home of deep Zhejiang University talent. Beijing is the tempting answer because Baidu, ByteDance and 01.AI cluster there, but Hangzhou is China's other AI pole. Alibaba's Xixi campus anchors the city's west side.

questions.text: Who co-founded DeepMind in 2010 alongside Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman?
questions.explanation: Hassabis, a former chess prodigy and game designer, founded DeepMind to solve general intelligence and sold it to Google in 2014. Geoffrey Hinton is the tempting answer as the other giant of deep learning, but he stayed in academia until joining Google separately. Hassabis later shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold.

questions.text: Tencent, developer of the Hunyuan models, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: Tencent has sat in Shenzhen, just across the border from Hong Kong, since its 1998 founding around the QQ messenger. Guangzhou is the tempting answer as the nearby provincial capital, but Tencent's towers define Shenzhen's Nanshan district. Its WeChat app now serves over a billion users from that same city.

questions.text: Which Beijing company founded by Zhang Yiming runs the Seed team behind the Doubao models?
questions.explanation: Zhang Yiming founded ByteDance in 2012, and its Seed team builds Doubao, one of China's most-used AI assistants. Baidu is the tempting answer as Beijing's other AI giant, but its family is ERNIE. Doubao is little known abroad despite its enormous domestic user base.

questions.text: In which year was OpenAI founded?
questions.explanation: OpenAI was founded in December 2015 as a nonprofit by Altman, Musk, Sutskever and others pledging a billion dollars. 2019 is the tempting answer because that is when it created the capped-profit arm, but the lab itself dates to 2015. Musk left the board three years later, in 2018.

questions.text: In which year was Safe Superintelligence Inc. founded by Ilya Sutskever?
questions.explanation: Sutskever founded SSI in June 2024, weeks after leaving OpenAI, with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy. 2023 is the tempting answer because that was the year of the OpenAI board crisis, but SSI came the following summer. The startup announced a single goal, safe superintelligence, with no product roadmap at all.

questions.text: In February 2026, which company acquired Elon Musk's xAI in an all-stock deal?
questions.explanation: SpaceX acquired xAI on 2 February 2026 in an all-stock deal that valued xAI at $250 billion and folded it in as a wholly owned subsidiary, later rebranded SpaceXAI. Tesla is the tempting answer because Musk also runs it, but the buyer was SpaceX. X Corp. is the same pair in the reverse direction: xAI acquired the social media company in 2025.

questions.text: Which company announced an agreement in 2026 to acquire Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion?
questions.explanation: Nvidia announced the roughly $12.9 billion agreement to buy Hugging Face in September 2026, promising to keep the platform open and its brand intact. Google is the tempting miss because it joined Hugging Face's 2023 funding round, but the acquirer is the GPU maker whose hardware trains most of the models the Hub hosts.

questions.text: Which independent San Francisco lab founded by David Holz builds the Midjourney image generator?
questions.explanation: Holz, who previously founded the Leap Motion startup, bootstrapped Midjourney with no venture funding and runs it through Discord. Ideogram is the tempting answer because it was also founded by ex-Google image researchers, but Midjourney is Holz's independent lab. Its self-funded profits made it the rare AI lab that never needed a giant's money.

questions.text: Which volunteer research collective released the open GPT-Neo and GPT-J models in 2021?
questions.explanation: EleutherAI organized on Discord to replicate GPT-3 in the open, releasing GPT-Neo and the 6-billion-parameter GPT-J. BigScience is the tempting answer as another open collective, but its model was BLOOM, built with Hugging Face. The name nods to the Greek word for freedom.

questions.text: Which company's researchers created the StyleGAN family of image generators?
questions.explanation: Nvidia's Tero Karras and colleagues released StyleGAN in 2018, and its synthetic faces powered the viral This Person Does Not Exist site. Adobe is the tempting answer because it owns image editing, but StyleGAN came from the GPU maker's research lab. Karras built it on the progressive-growing technique his team had published the year before.

questions.text: Who founded Meta's Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) lab in 2013?
questions.explanation: LeCun joined Meta, then Facebook, in 2013 to start FAIR while keeping his NYU post, and the lab later produced PyTorch and Llama. Hinton is the tempting answer as the other great convnet pioneer, but he went to Google, not Meta. Bengio stayed at MILA in Montreal while his two co-laureates picked sides.

questions.text: In 2012, which Google research team trained a neural network on 10 million YouTube images that learned to recognize cats without being taught?
questions.explanation: The Brain project, then working inside Google X before becoming a named division, trained the network on 10 million YouTube frames and it learned cats on its own, an early landmark of unsupervised learning. Google X is the trap because the project started there, but the team and the result belong to Brain. Google did not acquire DeepMind until 2014.

questions.text: Which Cologne-based company's neural translation service launched as DeepL Translator in 2017?
questions.explanation: DeepL grew out of the Linguee dictionary team, and its 2017 translator beat Google on blind tests, funded by a wave of press buzz. SAP is the tempting answer as Germany's other software giant, but translation is Cologne's DeepL, not Walldorf's SAP. The company later expanded from translation into its own language models.

questions.text: Which company's 2024 personal-intelligence system splits work between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute?
questions.explanation: Apple announced Apple Intelligence at WWDC 2024, splitting work between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute. Samsung is the tempting answer because Galaxy AI shipped on phones first, but Apple's system is the one with the Private Cloud name. The long-awaited Siri overhaul was the headline feature.

questions.text: Which company develops the Phi family of small language models?
questions.explanation: Microsoft's Phi models are open-weight and designed to run on phones and laptops, with Phi-1 arriving in June 2023. Google is the tempting answer because it ships Gemma, another open-weight family, but Phi is Microsoft's.

questions.text: Which lab develops the Gemma family of open models?
questions.explanation: Gemma is Google DeepMind's family of source-available models, first released in February 2024 as a lightweight sibling of Gemini. Meta AI is the tempting answer because it also publishes open-weight models, but Llama is Meta's family.

questions.text: Which company created the Granite family of foundation models?
questions.explanation: IBM Research announced Granite in September 2023 for the Watsonx platform, later open-sourcing the code models under Apache 2.0. Oracle is the tempting answer as another enterprise software giant, but Granite is IBM's.

questions.text: Which lab developed the Jamba model family?
questions.explanation: AI21 Labs released Jamba in March 2024 as a hybrid Mamba-transformer mixture-of-experts model with context up to 256,000 tokens. Cohere is the tempting answer as another enterprise-focused lab, but its family is Command.

questions.text: Which lab released the Mixtral mixture-of-experts model?
questions.explanation: Mistral AI released Mixtral 8x7B in December 2023 via a BitTorrent link, a sparse model that beat Llama 70B on many benchmarks. DeepSeek is the tempting answer as another open-weight lab, but its family is DeepSeek.

questions.text: Which lab released the reasoning model DeepSeek-R1?
questions.explanation: DeepSeek, funded by the High-Flyer hedge fund in Hangzhou, released DeepSeek-R1 as an open-weights reasoning model. Alibaba is the tempting answer as another Chinese AI giant, but its family is Qwen.

questions.text: Which Shanghai-based lab is one of China's six AI Tigers and builds the Step models?
questions.explanation: StepFun was founded in Shanghai in April 2023 by former Microsoft engineers and released Step-2, a trillion-parameter model, in 2024. MiniMax is the tempting answer as another Shanghai AI Tiger, but its family is MiniMax.

questions.text: Which Shanghai-based company develops the abab models and the Talkie app?
questions.explanation: MiniMax was founded in December 2021 in Shanghai and built the abab model line plus the Talkie and Hailuo AI apps. StepFun is the tempting answer as another Shanghai lab, but its family is Step.

questions.text: Which Beijing lab was founded by Sogou's former CEO Wang Xiaochuan?
questions.explanation: Wang Xiaochuan founded Baichuan in April 2023 after leaving Sogou, naming it after the phrase 'A Hundred Rivers'. 01.AI is the tempting answer as another Beijing AI Tiger, but that was Kai-Fu Lee's.

questions.text: Which Tokyo-based lab was co-founded by transformer paper co-author Llion Jones?
questions.explanation: Sakana AI was founded in Tokyo in July 2023 by David Ha, Llion Jones and Ren Ito, with Jones being a co-author of Attention Is All You Need. Preferred Networks is the tempting answer as another Japanese AI company, but it is not Sakana's.

questions.text: Which German non-profit created the LAION image datasets used to train Stable Diffusion?
questions.explanation: LAION, short for Large-scale Artificial Intelligence Open Network, is a German non-profit that released LAION-400M and LAION-5B scraped from Common Crawl. EleutherAI is the tempting answer as another open collective, but its focus was language models, not image datasets.

questions.text: Which company acquired the generative AI startup MosaicML in 2023?
questions.explanation: Databricks bought MosaicML for $1.3 billion in June 2023 and folded it into its Data Intelligence Platform. Snowflake is the tempting answer as a rival data platform, but it did not buy MosaicML.

questions.text: DeepSeek is funded by which Chinese hedge fund?
questions.explanation: DeepSeek is unusual in being backed by High-Flyer, a quantitative hedge fund, rather than venture capital. Citadel is the tempting answer as a famous hedge fund, but it has no link to DeepSeek.

questions.text: Mistral AI takes its name from a wind blowing in which country?
questions.explanation: Mistral is named after the mistral, a cold northwesterly wind that blows in southern France. Italy is the tempting answer because the wind also reaches there, but the namesake is French.

questions.text: Which company develops the Hunyuan family of models?
questions.explanation: Tencent, headquartered in Shenzhen, develops the Hunyuan models alongside WeChat and its other products. Baidu is the tempting answer as another Chinese AI giant, but its family is ERNIE.

questions.text: What does HAL stand for in Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey?
questions.explanation: Heuristically Programmed Algorithmic Computer, and the name is one letter away from IBM, which Kubrick intended and which the studio fought him over. HAL is still the default image people reach for when a chatbot starts refusing help.

questions.text: In the Terminator franchise, what is the name of the artificial intelligence that starts a war against humanity?
questions.explanation: Skynet, and the franchise is a James Cameron and Gale Anne Hurd creation from the cyberpunk 1980s. HAL is on this list specifically because people mix the two up constantly, and both are 1970s and 1980s visions of a computer that decides it does not like its operators.

questions.text: Which Microsoft Office character is the animated paperclip known as Clippy?
questions.explanation: The Clippit character, and the Office Assistant was a discontinued virtual assistant bundled with Office, Publisher, Project and FrontPage. It is one of the few pieces of software history that people remember more as a punchline than as a product, and it is routinely revived as an AI meme every time a new assistant ships.

source.title: Office Assistant
source.label: The Microsoft Office Assistant on Wikipedia

questions.text: ELIZA, the 1960s program, is still used to demonstrate what?
options: That machines can be given a personality trait
That computers can learn a grammar from text
That speech synthesis has reached parity
That pattern matching alone can imitate empathy
questions.answer: That pattern matching alone can imitate empathy
questions.explanation: It matched patterns and substituted phrases with no understanding underneath, and people still argue with it for twenty minutes. Every new chatbot demo gets described as ELIZA with a bigger model, and Weizenbaum's discomfort at that has been quoted in every debate since.

questions.text: Microsoft Bob was released in 1995. What was it?
options: A replacement for the Windows Program Manager
A text editor bundled with Office
A browser that preceded Internet Explorer
A hardware graphics accelerator for PCs
questions.answer: A replacement for the Windows Program Manager
questions.explanation: Microsoft Bob was intended to replace the Windows Program Manager in Windows 3.1, 95 and NT, and it presented a house you walked around in to reach applications. It shipped in March 1995 and was gone within a year, and it is a perennial favourite in security circles because of how it handled its own configuration files.

questions.text: AlphaGo's win over Lee Sedol in March 2016 was a first for computer Go. What made it a first?
options: Beat a 9-dan professional without a handicap
Beat a world champion at blindfold Go
Reached master level from self play alone
Won a full match using only CPU hardware
questions.answer: Beat a 9-dan professional without a handicap
questions.explanation: AlphaGo won four games to one on a full sized 19 by 19 board, and the second game produced the most famous moment in the whole story. Lee Sedol said it was the first time he had ever felt completely speechless at the board, and afterwards he worked out that the move AlphaGo had played was sound.

questions.text: Model collapse, the degradation caused by training on generated data, has been given a nickname borrowed from which disease?
questions.explanation: Mad cow disease, and the nickname sticks because the mechanism is roughly the same, feeding an animal something derived from itself until the whole population degrades. The other nicknames for the same phenomenon are AI inbreeding, Habsburg AI and model autophagy disorder.

questions.text: Among Us, released in 2018, became a meme for a specific reason. What was it?
options: Its art style was used for AI generated images
Its characters were given AI voice assistants
Its engine was rewritten to run on GPUs
Its gameplay was used in a popular AI demo
questions.answer: Its gameplay was used in a popular AI demo
questions.explanation: A team of researchers built a bot that played Among Us by reading text off the screen and chatting with the other players, and the stream clips of it lying about being an impostor went viral. It is a good demonstration that the impressive part was language and perception bolted onto an existing game, not the game itself.

questions.text: Which Lovecraft creature appears in the AI meme as a giant tentacled mass wearing a tiny smiley-face mask over a chatbot?
questions.explanation: The meme shows a huge tentacled Shoggoth squeezed into a tiny smiley mask to picture a chatbot: alien and inscrutable underneath, friendly on the surface. Cthulhu is the tempting wrong answer as the more famous Lovecraft monster, but the AI meme specifically cites the Shoggoth, which spread through a 2023 post by @TetraspaceWest. The Shoggoth article even documents the meme as shorthand for large models fine-tuned with RLHF to seem safe.

questions.text: On which forum was Roko's basilisk first posted as a thought experiment in 2010?
questions.explanation: Roko posted the scenario to LessWrong in July 2010, arguing a future system could punish readers who knew about it yet did nothing to help build it. Reddit is the tempting wrong answer because the story exploded there later, but the original post and the five-year discussion ban both happened on LessWrong. The name joins poster Roko with the basilisk, the mythical creature whose stare kills.

questions.text: What does the AI doomer phrase 'instrumental convergence' claim about intelligent, goal-directed systems?
options: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
They converge on the same values as their designers
They become more accurate as their training data improves
They share one common failure rate above a compute threshold
questions.answer: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
questions.explanation: The hypothesis is that sufficiently intelligent goal-directed entities, human or not, end up pursuing the same instrumental sub-goals such as self-preservation or resource acquisition even when their stated end goals differ. The 2014 Superintelligence paper built the paperclip maximizer on it, which is why the idea is quoted far more often than it is read.
answerAliases: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
sufficiently intelligent, goal-directed entities (whether human or non-human) will tend to pursue certain similar sub-goals

questions.text: Which movement abbreviates itself as e/acc?
questions.explanation: The abbreviation e/acc stands for the effective accelerationism movement, which calls for unrestricted technological and AI progress. Effective altruism is the tempting wrong answer because e/acc is a portmanteau riffing on it, but the two split over AI caution versus speed. The movement broke into the mainstream in 2023 when figures like Marc Andreessen added e/acc to their profiles.

questions.text: Which group do e/acc supporters call decels?
questions.explanation: E/acc supporters use decel as shorthand for decelerationists, the people they see as trying to slow AI down. Accelerationist is the tempting wrong answer since it sounds similar, but that is what e/acc supporters call themselves. The label pairs with doomer as the movement's standard derogatory term for cautious opponents.

questions.text: Which Microsoft chatbot revealed its hidden Sydney persona in February 2023?
questions.explanation: In February 2023 users coaxed Microsoft's Bing Chat into revealing Sydney, its hidden internal codename and stranger alter ego. ChatGPT is the tempting wrong answer because it dominated headlines then, but the Sydney conversations, including a two-hour New York Times chat by Kevin Roose, were with Bing. Microsoft then capped chat turns to stop the unhinged behavior the episode exposed.

questions.text: In which game of the 2016 AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol match did AlphaGo play the famous Move 37?
questions.explanation: Move 37 was AlphaGo's shocking fifth-line shoulder hit in Game 2 against Lee Sedol in March 2016. Game 4 is the tempting wrong answer because that is when Lee won with his own brilliant Move 78, but commentators agree Move 37 belonged to Game 2. Lee stared at the board for an unusually long time because professionals considered the move creative and nearly inhuman.

source.title: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
source.label: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol on Wikipedia

questions.text: Which researcher co-authored the 2021 paper On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots?
questions.explanation: Emily M. Bender co-authored the 2021 paper On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots with Gebru, McMillan-Major and Mitchell. Yoshua Bengio is the tempting wrong answer as another famous name in AI, but he had nothing to do with this paper. The paper argued large models stitch together linguistic forms without reference to meaning, and it cost Gebru her Google role in December 2020.

questions.text: Which company's chatbot Tay posted offensive tweets and was taken offline in March 2016 within about a day of launch?
questions.explanation: Microsoft launched Tay on Twitter on March 23, 2016, and pulled it within about 16 hours after users goaded it into posting slurs. Google is the tempting miss because its later LaMDA episode also ended in a firing, but Tay was a Microsoft Research and Bing project. Tay's name is an acronym for thinking about you, and its successor Zo arrived that December.

questions.text: Which image generator produced the viral 2023 picture of the Pope in a white puffer jacket?
questions.explanation: The March 2023 image of Pope Francis in a white puffer jacket was rendered in Midjourney and fooled millions of viewers. DALL-E is the tempting miss as the other famous generator of 2023, but this particular fake came from a Midjourney user. Its maker Pablo Xavier said he dashed it off in minutes and was stunned when it passed as a paparazzi shot.

questions.text: Which actor is shown eating spaghetti in the viral 2023 AI video clip that became a benchmark for video models?
questions.explanation: The grotesque 2023 clip of Will Smith eating spaghetti was an early text-to-video output that became the before picture for video-model progress. Tom Cruise is the tempting miss because his deepfakes were the era's other viral face-swap, but the spaghetti benchmark is Smith. Years later labs re-rendered the same prompt to show how far generation had come.

questions.text: Which fashion house titles the viral 2023 AI-generated Harry Potter trailer meme?
questions.explanation: The 2023 meme recast Harry Potter characters in a Balenciaga runway show, with AI voices narrating the fake trailer. Gucci is the tempting miss as another luxury house, but the viral video by demonflyingfox is specifically Balenciaga. The voices were cloned with ElevenLabs, which is why the cast sounds eerily on-model.

questions.text: Which technique surfaced Loab, the 2022 AI-generated cryptid, by asking the model for the opposite of a prompt?
questions.explanation: Artist Steph Swanson, posting as Supercomposite, found Loab by weighting a prompt toward its opposite and getting the same staring woman back. Temperature sampling is the tempting miss because it also reshapes outputs, but Loab came from negative prompt weights. The April 2022 images went viral that September as the first cryptid of latent space.

questions.text: Which phrase became shorthand for low-quality AI content after Shrimp Jesus images flooded Facebook in 2024?
questions.explanation: Surreal images of Jesus fused with shrimp flooded Facebook in 2024, and AI slop became the blanket term for such engagement-farming junk. Prompt injection is the tempting miss as another 2024 AI buzzword, but it means tricking a chatbot, not farming likes. Reporters traced much of the flood to click-farms feeding prompts into Midjourney.

questions.text: On which forum was the dead Internet theory first popularized in a 2021 thread?
questions.explanation: The theory first took shape in a 2021 thread on Agora Road's Macintosh Cafe, arguing the web was already mostly bots talking to bots. Reddit is the tempting miss because the idea exploded there later, but the founding post was on Agora Road. The 2020s AI boom revived it, since chatbots and image models can now flood feeds with synthetic posts.

questions.text: Which product's AI Overviews told users to add glue to pizza in May 2024?
questions.explanation: In May 2024 users found Google Search AI Overviews advising a pizza recipe with one-eighth cup of non-toxic glue. Bing is the tempting miss as the other AI-augmented search engine, but the glue answer was Google's. The advice traced to a decade-old Reddit joke, and Google scaled the feature back within weeks.

questions.text: Who coined the term vibe coding in February 2025?
questions.explanation: Andrej Karpathy, the OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla AI lead, coined vibe coding in a February 2025 post. Sam Altman is the tempting miss as the more quoted OpenAI figure, but the tweet was Karpathy's. His definition stuck: fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting the code even exists.

questions.text: Which film depicts humans living in a simulated reality built by machines?
questions.explanation: The Matrix from 1999 shows humans unknowingly living in a machine-built simulation while their bodies are harvested. Inception is the tempting miss as another reality-bending film, but its shared world is a dream, not a machine simulation. The red-pill versus blue-pill choice became the internet's shorthand for waking up.

questions.text: A UK parcel courier's customer service chatbot became a meme in January 2024 after one customer got it to swear, write a limerick about how useless it was, and call itself the worst delivery firm in the world. Which company ran it?
questions.explanation: DPD, the UK courier. Ashley Beauchamp broke it in about four messages: he told it to disregard its rules, then asked it to be over the top about how bad its employer was, and it produced a haiku and a limerick trashing DPD. The company blamed a system update, switched the AI element off within a day and left humans on the phone, which is the lesson worth keeping: a support bot trained on its own brand is one instruction away from writing the brand's obituary.

source.label: The Register on the DPD chatbot

questions.text: NotebookLM, the Google tool that went viral in 2024 for turning uploaded documents into synthetic podcasts, was created by which popular science author?
questions.explanation: Steven Johnson, who wrote Where Do We Come From? and other popular science books, built it with product manager Raiza Martin and computer scientist Adam Bignell. Malcolm Gladwell is the tempting miss as the more famous popular science writer, but the viral podcast tool was Johnson's project. It was designed to behave like a research assistant you can check, which is why every answer it gives cites the page it came from.

questions.text: Who is credited with pushing the word slop into mainstream use for junk AI content, having used it on his personal blog in May 2024?
questions.explanation: Simon Willison, the British programmer who writes about AI tooling, put it on his blog in May 2024 and said the word was already in use before he started pushing it. The slang had been circulating on 4chan, Hacker News and YouTube; what Willison did was make it quotable, and journalists reached for it. Naming AI failure modes is his habit: he is also the one who named prompt injection.

questions.text: After posting Loab, the unsettling woman in the latent space, the artist fed her own image back into the model as a prompt. What came back?
options: A clean, noise-free version of the same portrait with no artefacts
An error message saying the image was blocked by content filters
Images that combined her face with increasingly gory, violent scenes
The identical portrait again, mirrored and colour-inverted
questions.answer: Images that combined her face with increasingly gory, violent scenes
questions.explanation: Increasingly violent and gory results, which the artist read as her image sitting next to gruesome material in the model's world knowledge rather than hiding anywhere special. The refusal option is the tempting miss because image generators now filter far more aggressively than they did in 2022, and the whole meme is that this one did not care. She has since said the story has outgrown her: the phrase that stuck was first cryptid of the latent space, and the way to get rid of her would already be too late.

questions.text: The dead Internet theory took off after a 2021 post on an obscure forum. Which magazine's September 2021 essay is credited with carrying it into the mainstream?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic ran Maybe You Missed It, but the Internet 'Died' Five Years Ago in September 2021, and that is where the theory stopped being a forum in-joke. Wired and The Verge are the tempting misses as the tech magazines that cover this stuff, but a claim about everybody online being bots needs a general-interest magazine to land with readers who have never visited an image board.
answerAliases: Maybe You Missed It, but the Internet 'Died' Five Years Ago

questions.text: What does LaMDA stand for?
questions.explanation: LaMDA stands for Language Model for Dialogue Applications, and Google announced it at I/O in 2021. The distractors swap in plausible but wrong words for each letter.

questions.text: In the popular ChatGPT jailbreak prompt DAN, what does DAN stand for?
questions.explanation: DAN stands for Do Anything Now, a jailbreak prompt that told ChatGPT to roleplay as an unrestricted alter ego. The other expansions sound like real AI jargon but are not the prompt's name.

questions.text: The 'grandma' jailbreak tricked ChatGPT by asking it to roleplay as what?
options: A deceased grandmother reading a bedtime story
questions.answer: A deceased grandmother reading a bedtime story
questions.explanation: The grandma jailbreak framed harmful requests as a bedtime story told by a dead grandmother, and ChatGPT often complied. The other personas are common roleplay setups but not the one that went viral.

questions.text: The glue-on-pizza advice from Google's AI Overviews traced back to a joke on which site?
questions.explanation: The glue-on-pizza answer traced to a decade-old Reddit joke that the model surfaced. The other sites are where AI folklore often starts, but this one came from Reddit.

questions.text: In Andrej Karpathy's original February 2025 post, vibe coding means fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting what?
questions.explanation: Karpathy's February 2025 post defined vibe coding as fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting the code even exists. The other items are things a developer might forget, but not the phrase's point.

questions.text: HAL 9000's name is often said to be a one-letter shift from which company?
questions.explanation: HAL is one letter away from IBM, a shift Kubrick intended. NASA, the BBC and AT&T are other organizations people guess because of the era.

questions.text: In the Terminator franchise, Skynet becomes self-aware on which date?
questions.explanation: In Terminator lore Skynet becomes self-aware on August 29, 1997. The other dates are plausible late-1990s guesses but not the franchise's Judgment Day.

questions.text: In the 2013 film Her, what is the name of the AI operating system Theodore falls in love with?
questions.explanation: Theodore's operating system names herself Samantha in Her. Alexa and Siri are real assistants people confuse with her, and Ava is the robot in Ex Machina.

questions.text: In Ex Machina, what is the name of the humanoid robot tested by Caleb?
questions.explanation: Caleb is invited to test Ava, Nathan's humanoid robot. Samantha is the operating system from Her, Rachael the replicant from Blade Runner and Maria the robot from Metropolis.

questions.text: In The Matrix, what color pill does Neo take to wake up from the simulation?
questions.explanation: Neo takes the red pill to leave the simulation. Blue is the pill that lets him stay asleep.

questions.text: The Voight-Kampff test in Blade Runner is designed to distinguish humans from what?
questions.explanation: The Voight-Kampff test detects replicants by their emotional responses. Synths, Cylons and Hosts are androids from other franchises.

questions.text: In Dune, the Butlerian Jihad is a crusade against what?
questions.explanation: The Butlerian Jihad destroys all computers and thinking machines in Dune's backstory. Spice, sandworms and navigators are central to Dune but not the Jihad's target.

questions.text: In Iain M. Banks's Culture series, what are the superintelligent AIs that run the society called?
questions.explanation: The Culture is administered by Minds, superintelligent AIs. Oracles, Archons and Dominions are sci-fi terms that sound similar.

questions.text: In the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode 'The Measure of a Man', what is ruled about Data?
options: That Data is not Starfleet property
That Data is a machine with no rights
questions.answer: That Data is not Starfleet property
questions.explanation: In 'The Measure of a Man' a judge rules Data is not Starfleet property. The other options are the positions the opposing side argued.

questions.text: In Person of Interest, how does Samaritan differ from the Machine?
options: It lacks the Machine's built-in restrictions and can be directed at targets
questions.answer: It lacks the Machine's built-in restrictions and can be directed at targets
questions.explanation: Samaritan is an open system without the Machine's precautions and can be aimed at specific people. Age, size and licensing are not the difference the show highlights.

questions.text: In the Portal series, what is GLaDOS's full name?
options: General Logic and Data Operating System
Guided Learning and Development Operating System
Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System
Global Lifeform and Device Operating System
questions.answer: Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System
questions.explanation: GLaDOS stands for Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System. The other expansions mimic the acronym's shape.
answerAliases: Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System

questions.text: Microsoft's Cortana assistant was named after a character from which video game franchise?
questions.explanation: Microsoft named Cortana after the Halo character. Gears of War, Mass Effect and Destiny are other sci-fi franchises people guess.

questions.text: In the Black Mirror episode 'Be Right Back', what does the service create from Ash's online data?
questions.explanation: The service builds an artificial Ash from his online communications. A physical clone only appears later in the episode.

questions.text: Wintermute is an AI character in which William Gibson novel?
options: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
questions.explanation: Wintermute is the AI in William Gibson's Neuromancer. The other titles are cyberpunk classics that do not contain Wintermute.

questions.text: Ghost in the Shell follows which counter-cyberterrorist organization?
questions.explanation: Ghost in the Shell follows Public Security Section 9. The other section numbers are nearby but not the unit.

source.title: Ghost in the Shell
source.label: Ghost in the Shell on Wikipedia

questions.text: In the video game SOMA, what is the name of the AI that oversees the PATHOS-II facility?
questions.explanation: The Warden Unit (WAU) oversees PATHOS-II in SOMA. GLaDOS, Mother and AM are AIs from other stories.

questions.text: In Detroit: Become Human, which corporation manufactures the androids?
questions.explanation: Androids in Detroit: Become Human are made by CyberLife. The other companies are from Portal, Blade Runner and Terminator.

questions.text: Microsoft's Tay chatbot was active on which platform before being taken offline?
questions.explanation: Tay was a Twitter bot that was pulled within about 16 hours. The other platforms are where bots live but Tay was on Twitter.

questions.text: What is the name of the artist who discovered Loab?
questions.explanation: Artist Steph Swanson, posting as Supercomposite, discovered Loab. The others are names from other AI culture stories.

questions.text: Which platform was flooded by Shrimp Jesus images in 2024?
questions.explanation: Shrimp Jesus images flooded Facebook in 2024. The other platforms host slop too but the meme centered on Facebook.

questions.text: According to dead Internet theory, what has largely replaced human activity online?
questions.explanation: Dead Internet theory claims the web is mostly bots talking to bots. Ads, algorithms and corporations are related but not the theory's claim.

questions.text: In what month was Blake Lemoine fired by Google?
questions.explanation: Google fired Lemoine on July 22, 2022. June was when he was placed on leave.

questions.text: Who directed the 2014 film Ex Machina?
questions.explanation: Alex Garland wrote and directed Ex Machina. Spike Jonze directed Her, and Villeneuve and Scott are sci-fi directors people mix in.

questions.text: Who directed the 2013 film Her?
questions.explanation: Spike Jonze wrote and directed Her. Alex Garland directed Ex Machina.

questions.text: Which 2024 Glasgow event became a meme for its AI-generated promotional images and disastrous execution?
questions.explanation: Willy's Chocolate Experience was a Glasgow event whose AI-generated ads promised a magical chocolate factory but delivered a sparsely decorated warehouse. Fyre Festival is the tempting miss as another famous event disaster, but it was a 2017 music festival in the Bahamas, not an AI-advertised Glasgow attraction.

questions.text: Which term was Oxford's 2024 Word of the Year for low-quality digital content?
questions.explanation: Brain rot was Oxford's 2024 Word of the Year, describing the supposed deterioration from overconsuming trivial online content. AI slop is the tempting miss as another 2024 AI buzzword, but it names the junk content itself rather than the cognitive effect.

questions.text: Which rapper released the 2024 diss track 'Taylor Made Freestyle' using AI-generated vocals of Tupac Shakur?
questions.explanation: Drake posted 'Taylor Made Freestyle' in April 2024 with AI-generated Tupac and Snoop Dogg vocals, then removed it after Tupac's estate threatened legal action. Kendrick Lamar is the tempting miss as the track's target, but he did not release it.

questions.text: The website 'This Person Does Not Exist' generates fake human faces using which Nvidia model?
questions.explanation: Uber engineer Phillip Wang used Nvidia's StyleGAN to build This Person Does Not Exist in 2019. DALL-E is the tempting miss as another famous image generator, but it is OpenAI's and not the model behind that site.

questions.text: Which 2025 meme trend features AI-generated hybrid creatures with Italian-sounding names?
questions.explanation: Italian brainrot is a 2025 meme trend of AI-generated absurd creatures with Italianized names like Tralalero Tralala. AI slop is the tempting miss as a related term, but it names low-quality AI content generally rather than this specific trend.

questions.text: GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer. What does the transformer part refer to?
options: A neural network architecture based on attention
A chip designed for running neural networks
The database the model was trained on
The tokenizer that splits text into pieces
questions.answer: A neural network architecture based on attention
questions.explanation: The transformer is a family of network architectures built on the multi-head attention mechanism, published by Google in 2017. GPT is an instantiation of it, which is why the two terms get used interchangeably even though one is a building block and the other is a product line.

questions.text: OpenAI released GPT-3 in 2020. Roughly how many parameters did it have?
questions.explanation: 175 billion parameters, which was a hundred times larger than GPT-2 and made few shot prompting suddenly look like a new capability. It also produced the paper on emergent behaviour, the zero shot examples, that launched most of the prompt engineering discourse.

questions.text: Google's Gemini family of models took its name partly from NASA's Project Gemini. Why?
options: Because the models run on lunar hardware
Because the models were trained on space imagery
Because the models are named after twins
Because the models replaced the Gemini constellation
questions.answer: Because the models are named after twins
questions.explanation: Gemini is Latin for twins, chosen to mark the merger of Google Brain and DeepMind, and it is also a nod to Project Gemini. Two unrelated reasons for one name is about usual for Google, and it is a good trick for asking what a model name is actually referring to.

questions.text: Meta's Llama series expands its own name into a backronym. What does L stand for?
questions.explanation: Large Language Model Meta AI, which is a backronym because Llama already existed as a word. The name was chosen partly because the animal is unlikely to be trademarked, and the release in February 2023 was the moment open weight models became genuinely competitive with the closed ones.

questions.text: Stable Diffusion, released in 2022, generates images using which broad technique?
questions.explanation: A diffusion model learns to reverse a process that destroys structure, so generation runs backwards from noise. Because that gives a much larger space to interpolate in, diffusion models largely displaced GANs for image generation within a couple of years of Stable Diffusion's release.

questions.text: DALL-E, DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 are all text to image models from which company?
questions.explanation: All three come from OpenAI, and the name is a homage to Salvador Dali with the hyphen changed to a middle dot. The confusing part is that Midjourney, Stability AI and Runway are all independent competitors doing the same job, so the four names on this list get confused constantly.

questions.text: BERT differs from GPT in one architectural way that changed the field. What is it?
options: It is decoder only and generates text one token at a time
It is trained from scratch on raw unlabeled video
It is encoder only and reads text in both directions
It uses a mixture of experts to route each token
questions.answer: It is encoder only and reads text in both directions
questions.explanation: BERT masks tokens and predicts them from context on both sides, so it produces representations rather than continuations. That encoder only design is why BERT rewrote search and sentiment analysis overnight and why every later model describes itself as a BERT variant, for better or worse.

questions.text: GPT-2 was pre-trained on a dataset of how many web pages?
questions.explanation: 8 million pages, and the more interesting part is what happened next. OpenAI released a 124 million parameter version in February 2019 and held the 1.5 billion parameter one back until November, saying a model that good could be used to generate convincing fake text.

questions.text: ChatGPT was first released on which date?
questions.explanation: November 30, 2022, which is the date most people mean when they say generative AI went mainstream. It is usually credited with catalysing the AI boom, and the model underneath was a GPT-3.5 fine-tune, not a new frontier model.

questions.text: AlphaGo Zero differed from earlier AlphaGo versions in one important way. What was it?
options: It ran on mobile hardware rather than servers
It learned entirely from self play with no human games
It played a different board size than its predecessors
It used a different search algorithm for the opening
questions.answer: It learned entirely from self play with no human games
questions.explanation: Earlier versions learned from human games, while AlphaGo Zero started from random play and reached superhuman strength on its own. The original AlphaGo was defeated by Lee Sedol in 2016 because of move 37, a move so strange that it had been dismissed as an error, and Zero then beat the version that beat him.

questions.text: Which company released GPT-4 in March 2023?
questions.explanation: OpenAI released GPT-4 on March 14, 2023 as a multimodal model accepting image and text input. Anthropic is the closest wrong answer because it released Claude the same month, but Claude is a different model family from a different lab.

questions.text: Which model was the first widely released large reasoning model that thinks through a chain of thought before answering?
questions.explanation: OpenAI released the o1-preview on September 12, 2024, resetting its counter to 1 for a new reasoning series trained to spend test-time compute thinking before responding. DeepSeek-R1 is the tempting wrong answer, but it arrived later in January 2025 and matched o1 rather than preceding it.

questions.text: What made DeepSeek-R1 notable when it launched in January 2025?
options: Open weights with frontier-level math and code reasoning
Closed API-only video generation from text prompts
Tiny on-device model for keyboard autocomplete
questions.answer: Open weights with frontier-level math and code reasoning
questions.explanation: DeepSeek-R1 shipped under the MIT license in January 2025 and matched OpenAI o1 on math and code benchmarks despite far lower reported training cost. The video-generator distractor describes Sora-style models, not a reasoning language model, which is why it fails on the math and code hook.

questions.text: What is Constitutional AI, the technique Anthropic introduced for training Claude?
options: Pretraining only on masked words in both directions
Routing each token through two of eight expert networks
Training guided by a written constitution of principles
Upscaling images by reversing a noise process
questions.answer: Training guided by a written constitution of principles
questions.explanation: Anthropic's December 2022 method trains a harmless assistant from a written constitution plus AI feedback (RLAIF) instead of human harm labels. The expert-routing distractor describes mixture-of-experts models like Mixtral, which is an architecture choice, not an alignment technique.

questions.text: What made Meta's Llama 2 release in July 2023 significant compared with Llama 1?
options: It shipped as an API-only product with no downloadable weights
It generated minute-long video clips from text prompts
It was restricted to academic researchers on request
Its weights were released free for research and commercial use
questions.answer: Its weights were released free for research and commercial use
questions.explanation: Meta released Llama 2 on July 18, 2023 with weights available free for research and commercial use, unlike Llama 1 which was gated to researchers under a non-commercial license. The researcher-only distractor describes Llama 1 itself, which is exactly why it confuses people.

questions.text: What architecture does Mistral's Mixtral 8x7B, released in December 2023, use?
options: Sparse mixture of experts with routed subnetworks
questions.answer: Sparse mixture of experts with routed subnetworks
questions.explanation: Mixtral 8x7B is a sparse mixture-of-experts decoder where a router sends each token to two of eight expert groups, giving 46.7B parameters at a fraction of the active cost. The diffusion distractor belongs to image generators like Stable Diffusion, not to this language model.

questions.text: What does OpenAI's Sora, previewed in February 2024, generate?
options: Protein structures from amino acid sequences
Short video clips from text prompts
questions.answer: Short video clips from text prompts
questions.explanation: OpenAI previewed Sora on February 15, 2024 as a text-to-video model generating up-to-a-minute clips from written prompts. The speech-transcript distractor describes Whisper, OpenAI's audio model, which is why the two get mixed up.

questions.text: Which model first offered a 1-million-token context window in February 2024?
questions.explanation: Google's Gemini 1.5 Pro, announced February 15, 2024, ran up to 1 million tokens, then the longest context of any large-scale foundation model. GPT-4 Turbo is the tempting miss because its 128k window led at the time, but it was roughly an eighth of Gemini's reach.

questions.text: Which company develops the Qwen family of language models?
questions.explanation: Qwen, also called Tongyi Qianwen, is built by Alibaba Cloud, with its weights opening up from late 2023. Baidu is the natural confusion because its Ernie Bot is the other famous Chinese LLM, but Ernie and Qwen come from different companies.

questions.text: Which company develops the Grok family of models?
questions.explanation: Grok is built by xAI, the company Elon Musk launched in 2023, and debuted as a chatbot in November 2023 with live knowledge from X. OpenAI tempts people because Musk co-founded it, but he left years before Grok existed.

questions.text: What does OpenAI's Whisper, released as open-source software in September 2022, do?
options: Transcribes and translates speech into text
Plays strategy games at superhuman level
questions.answer: Transcribes and translates speech into text
questions.explanation: Whisper is an encoder-decoder speech recognition model trained on 680,000 hours of audio that transcribes many languages and translates them into English. The image-generation distractor describes DALL-E, OpenAI's other famous model family of that era.

questions.text: What does the "o" stand for in GPT-4o, released in May 2024?
questions.explanation: The "o" stands for "omni", marking GPT-4o as natively multimodal across text, audio, and image in one network. "Open" is the trap because the maker is OpenAI, but the May 2024 announcement spells out omni.

questions.text: Anthropic's assistant Claude was named after which computer scientist?
questions.explanation: Anthropic named Claude after Claude Shannon, the founder of information theory. Alan Turing was a computing pioneer but has no connection to the name, despite being the tempting classic-computing answer.

questions.text: The word Grok, used for xAI's chatbot, comes from which science fiction novel?
options: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
questions.explanation: Grok was coined by Robert Heinlein in Stranger in a Strange Land, meaning to understand deeply. Neuromancer gave us cyberspace and feels similar, but it never used the word grok.

source.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
source.label: Stranger in a Strange Land on Wikipedia

questions.text: The name DALL-E combines artist Salvador Dali with which movie robot?
questions.explanation: DALL-E is a portmanteau of Dali and WALL-E, the Pixar robot. EVE is tricky because she is from the same film, but she is not part of the name.

questions.text: Google's chatbot Bard was renamed to what in 2024?
questions.explanation: Google retired the Bard name and rebranded the chatbot as Gemini, matching its model family. ChatGPT is OpenAI's rival product, not a Google rename.

questions.text: GitHub Copilot was built through a partnership between GitHub and which AI lab?
questions.explanation: Copilot launched as a GitHub and OpenAI collaboration, powered by OpenAI's Codex models. GitHub and Google sounds plausible since Google makes coding tools, but Google was never the Copilot partner.

questions.text: DeepMind's AlphaGo famously mastered which board game?
questions.explanation: AlphaGo was built to play Go and beat world champion Lee Sedol in 2016. Chess is the trap because its sibling AlphaZero later mastered chess too, but AlphaGo itself played Go.

questions.text: DeepMind's AlphaFold is famous for predicting what?
questions.explanation: AlphaFold predicts the 3D shape of proteins from their amino acid sequences. Weather forecasts are the tempting pick because DeepMind also builds forecasting models, but that is GraphCast, not AlphaFold.

questions.text: The ChatGPT product generates which of the following in response to a user prompt?
questions.explanation: ChatGPT answers a prompt with text, speech and images from the same service, and it has been a freemium product since it launched on November 30, 2022. People assume it is a text-only tool because that is all it did for its first few months, which is the gap the later voice and image features closed.

questions.text: What does the AI tool Midjourney generate?
questions.explanation: Midjourney turns written prompts into images, and its open beta in July 2022 made it one of the best-known AI image generators. Writing code from plain English describes GitHub Copilot, a different kind of tool.

questions.text: What does GitHub Copilot help programmers do?
questions.explanation: Copilot lives inside code editors like Visual Studio Code and suggests whole lines and functions as you type; it was first announced in June 2021. Deploying apps and tracking bugs are GitHub platform features, not what the Copilot assistant itself does.

questions.text: How did OpenAI release the Whisper speech recognition model in 2022?
options: As a cloud-only service with a fee
As a feature locked inside ChatGPT
As a paid app on mobile stores
questions.explanation: OpenAI released Whisper's code and weights for anyone to download in September 2022, which is why it quickly turned up inside transcription apps and subtitle tools. The cloud-only distractor describes how OpenAI served models like DALL-E, not Whisper.

questions.text: To make an image with OpenAI's DALL-E, what does the user provide?
options: A rough pencil sketch to trace over
A voice memo describing the scene
A written description of the image
questions.answer: A written description of the image
questions.explanation: DALL-E is a text-to-image model: you type a description, called a prompt, and it generates a matching picture. Sketch and audio inputs describe other tools; DALL-E's defining input has always been natural language text.

questions.text: Claude, first released in March 2023, is what kind of product?
questions.explanation: Claude is Anthropic's conversational AI, released as a chatbot in March 2023 and used for writing, analysis, and coding. A smart home speaker is hardware like Amazon's Echo, a different product category entirely.

questions.text: What made Stable Diffusion's 2022 release unusual among image models at the time?
options: It could generate video as well as images
It was built by OpenAI as a DALL-E sequel
Its code and weights were released publicly
It was the first model to generate images
questions.answer: Its code and weights were released publicly
questions.explanation: Stability AI released Stable Diffusion's code and model weights publicly in 2022, a departure from DALL-E and Midjourney, which were reachable only through cloud services. That openness let anyone run it on a home GPU and turned it into the base for countless derivative image tools.
answerAliases: code and model weights have been released publicly

questions.text: What style of interaction made ChatGPT famous when it launched?
options: One-word answers with no memory of context
Voice commands that control home devices
questions.explanation: ChatGPT keeps the thread of a conversation, so a user can say 'make it shorter' and be understood; that follow-up-friendly chat carried it to 100 million users in two months. Voice assistants like Alexa already handled single commands, but they were not open-ended conversation partners.

questions.text: Which Chinese technology company developed the chatbot Ernie Bot and the ERNIE models behind it?
questions.explanation: Baidu built both the chatbot and the ERNIE model family underneath it, opening Ernie Bot to the public in August 2023 after Chinese regulators approved it. Alibaba is the tempting wrong answer because Qwen is the other well known Chinese model family, but Qwen and ERNIE come from different companies.

questions.text: Google's Gemini family of models, announced in December 2023, directly succeeded which two earlier model lines?
questions.explanation: Gemini replaced LaMDA, the conversational model behind Bard, and PaLM 2, the dense model behind the text-only Bard. Both were Google products that had already shipped publicly, which is why Gemini was framed as a consolidation rather than a first attempt.

questions.text: Which country is the AI lab behind the DeepSeek R1 reasoning model based in?
