options: A contrastive loss that aligns image and text encoders
A retrieval index that fetches text chunks during generation
A flexible output query so one model can emit labels, text, pixels or flow fields
A mixture-of-experts layer that routes tokens to separate specialists
questions.answer: A flexible output query so one model can emit labels, text, pixels or flow fields
questions.explanation: Perceiver IO adds an output query array that cross-attends the latents, so the same encoder can produce a class label, a sentence, optical flow or raw pixels depending on the query. The mixture-of-experts distractor belongs to Switch Transformer, a different scaling story from earlier in 2021.

questions.text: How does the 2021 RETRO model use its two-trillion-token retrieval database when generating text?
options: It copies the single closest document verbatim as its answer
It retrieves relevant chunks and cross-attends to them while predicting the next tokens
It fine-tunes its weights on the retrieved chunks before each reply
It uses retrieval only to rerank answers after generation finishes
questions.answer: It retrieves relevant chunks and cross-attends to them while predicting the next tokens
questions.explanation: RETRO splits both the input and its giant corpus into chunks, retrieves neighbours of each chunk, and fuses them with chunked cross-attention as it predicts. It never retrains per query, which rules out the fine-tuning distractor, and retrieval happens during generation rather than as a post-hoc rerank.

questions.text: DeepMind's 2021 Gopher model was notable at release mainly for what?
options: Beating grandmasters at StarCraft II with no prior games
Generating images from text better than rival generators
Running on a single consumer graphics card
Its enormous dense scale, hundreds of billions of parameters, then near the frontier of model size
questions.answer: Its enormous dense scale, hundreds of billions of parameters, then near the frontier of model size
questions.explanation: Gopher packed 280 billion parameters into a dense transformer and matched or beat rivals on reading, fact-checking and reasoning tests. StarCraft belongs to AlphaStar, a different DeepMind project, and image generation was never Gopher's job.

questions.text: Google's 2022 PaLM paper trained a 540-billion-parameter model on two TPU v4 pods. What system made that training setup possible?
options: Pathways, which orchestrates training across thousands of accelerator chips
A single giant graphics card holding all the weights at once
Volunteer laptops donating idle compute over the internet
A purely CPU cluster with no accelerators at all
questions.answer: Pathways, which orchestrates training across thousands of accelerator chips
questions.explanation: Pathways let a single system spread one model across thousands of TPU chips with clever sharding, and the 540-billion-parameter PaLM run was its showcase. No single card could hold those weights, which is what makes the lone-GPU distractor physically impossible rather than merely unlikely.

questions.text: The 2022 UL2 paper unified pretraining objectives with a Mixture-of-Denoisers. What does that mixture combine?
options: Three separate models that vote on each answer at test time
Several span-corruption styles, from short masked spans to long aggressive ones
Human rankings mixed with AI-written critiques
Translation pairs mixed with image-caption pairs
questions.answer: Several span-corruption styles, from short masked spans to long aggressive ones
questions.explanation: UL2 frames every objective as corrupting spans and reconstructing them, mixing short regular gaps, longer aggressive ones and full-prefix generation so one model learns them all. The three-voting-models distractor is an ensemble, a test-time trick, while UL2 is a single pretraining recipe.

questions.text: The 2021 T0 paper showed strong zero-shot results on unseen tasks. What fine-tuning recipe produced that?
options: Training only on labelled sentiment reviews for sharper classifiers
Reinforcement learning from live user thumbs-down clicks
Multitask training on a large collection of prompted datasets with natural-language instructions
Distilling answers from a much larger proprietary teacher model
questions.answer: Multitask training on a large collection of prompted datasets with natural-language instructions
questions.explanation: T0 fine-tuned an encoder-decoder on dozens of datasets, each wrapped in many natural-language prompts, so new tasks arrive as just another instruction to read. The teacher-distillation distractor describes how smaller models later copied giants, not how T0 itself learned to follow instructions.

questions.text: The 176-billion-parameter BLOOM model was trained on ROOTS, a corpus built for the project. What made ROOTS distinctive?
options: It contained only English Wikipedia articles from a single year
It was generated entirely by an earlier language model
It held only Python code with no natural language
Web text gathered across dozens of natural and programming languages by hundreds of researchers
questions.answer: Web text gathered across dozens of natural and programming languages by hundreds of researchers
questions.explanation: ROOTS gathered web text across dozens of natural and programming languages through workshops of researchers who could document consent and provenance. An English-only Wikipedia scrape would have defeated BLOOM's whole multilingual purpose, and nothing in the corpus was machine-generated.

questions.text: OpenAI's 2022 Whisper paper took an unusual approach to speech-recognition data. What did it train on?
options: Hundreds of thousands of hours of audio with transcripts scraped from the web, used with minimal cleaning
A few hundred hours of studio recordings read by voice actors
Only synthetic speech generated by a text-to-speech system
Silent video clips with no audio track at all
questions.answer: Hundreds of thousands of hours of audio with transcripts scraped from the web, used with minimal cleaning
questions.explanation: Whisper learned from a vast haul of weakly labelled web audio, trading curation for scale, and that robustness is why it transcribes accents and background noise so well. Studio recordings are the old supervised recipe Whisper deliberately abandoned.

questions.text: The 2020 NeRF paper represents a 3D scene as what, so that new views can be rendered from any angle?
options: A hand-modelled mesh sculpted by artists in editing software
A neural network mapping 3D positions and viewing directions to color and density
A stack of photographs stapled together in angle order
A point cloud captured by an expensive laser scanner
questions.answer: A neural network mapping 3D positions and viewing directions to color and density
questions.explanation: NeRF fits a small neural network that outputs color and density for any 3D point seen from any direction, then renders views by marching rays through it. A hand-modelled mesh needs artists, which is exactly the labour NeRF removes.

questions.text: The 2021 Masked Autoencoders paper found vision transformers learn best when pretraining hides how much of each image?
options: Masking only one pixel in twenty
Masking three of every four patches
Masking everything but a thin border
questions.answer: Masking three of every four patches
questions.explanation: Masking three quarters of the patches forces the model to reason about whole objects from slivers, and the paper showed accuracy climbs as masking rises far past the small fractions used in language. Masking almost nothing would make reconstruction trivial copying, which teaches the encoder nothing.

questions.text: The 2020 SimCLR paper learns image representations without labels. What is its core training signal?
options: Predicting the publication year stamped on each photograph
Reconstructing every pixel of the input image exactly
Classifying each image into one of a thousand fixed categories
Pulling two augmented views of the same image together while pushing different images apart
questions.answer: Pulling two augmented views of the same image together while pushing different images apart
questions.explanation: Two random crops, color jitters and blurs of one image must land near each other in embedding space while other images are pushed away, and that tug-of-war alone learns features that rival supervised ones. The thousand-categories distractor is ImageNet classification, the labelled paradigm SimCLR was built to escape.

questions.text: The 2019 DistilBERT paper compressed BERT by knowledge distillation. What was the headline trade-off it reported?
options: Ten times larger than BERT with slightly better accuracy
About forty percent smaller and sixty percent faster while keeping most of BERT's accuracy
Identical size to BERT but trained on ten times more data
A vision model that replaced BERT for image tasks
questions.answer: About forty percent smaller and sixty percent faster while keeping most of BERT's accuracy
questions.explanation: A student network trained to mimic BERT's soft outputs kept nearly all of its benchmark performance at a fraction of the size and latency. A larger model would be the opposite of compression, which rules out the ten-times-larger distractor immediately.

questions.text: The 2019 ALBERT paper shrank BERT-style models with two tricks. Which pair did it introduce?
options: Factorized embeddings plus cross-layer sharing, with sentence-order prediction
Full attention replaced by fixed random projections in every layer
Removing all normalization layers and doubling the vocabulary
Training only on labelled sentiment data for sharper classifiers
questions.answer: Factorized embeddings plus cross-layer sharing, with sentence-order prediction
questions.explanation: ALBERT factorizes the embedding matrix and reuses the same weights across layers, then replaces next-sentence prediction with ordering two consecutive sentences correctly. Random projections describe a different efficiency family, not learned sharing.

questions.text: The 2021 Switch Transformer paper scaled past a trillion parameters efficiently. What routing rule defines it?
options: Every token is processed by every expert in parallel
Tokens are routed by a human-written rulebook per subject
A dense feedforward layer replaces all experts at test time
Each token is routed to exactly one expert chosen by a learned switch
questions.answer: Each token is routed to exactly one expert chosen by a learned switch
questions.explanation: A router sends each token to its single best expert, so capacity grows with expert count while compute per token stays flat, and the paper reached past a trillion parameters that way. Sending every token everywhere would cost as much as a dense model of that size, defeating the design.

questions.text: Google's 2021 GLaM model held over a trillion parameters across dozens of experts per layer. Why did it cost less energy to serve than a dense model of that size?
options: It deleted its largest layers before serving
It ran entirely on volunteer laptop CPUs
Only a small subset of experts activates for each token, so most weights sit idle per prediction
It answered every query from a cache of past responses
questions.answer: Only a small subset of experts activates for each token, so most weights sit idle per prediction
questions.explanation: GLaM holds over a trillion weights but wakes only a couple of experts per token, so each prediction costs a fraction of a dense giant's. The deleted-layers distractor confuses sparsity with amputation: the weights stay, they just take turns.

questions.text: Besides sensibleness, specificity and interestingness, the 2022 LaMDA paper scored replies against external knowledge sources. What was that metric called?
options: Parameter count of the serving model
Groundedness, whether replies stay consistent with known sources
Tokens generated per second on a phone
Number of languages the model can translate
questions.answer: Groundedness, whether replies stay consistent with known sources
questions.explanation: Alongside sensibleness and specificity, the paper scored groundedness against known sources, because a chatbot that sounds right but invents facts fails exactly where dialogue matters. Parameter count is a property of the model, not a grade of any reply.

questions.text: DeepMind's 2022 Sparrow paper built a dialogue agent that cites evidence. How did it ground its answers?
options: Live web search queries whose results the model must quote as supporting evidence
A hand-coded rulebook covering every tested science subject
Memorized passages with no live lookup at all
Paid crowdworkers rewriting every wrong answer by hand
questions.answer: Live web search queries whose results the model must quote as supporting evidence
questions.explanation: Sparrow issues live search queries and must support its claims with quotes from the results, with human rules shaping the ranking. Memorized passages would go stale and cannot be checked, which is why the paper insisted on browsing.

questions.text: The 2022 InstructGPT paper reported a striking preference result. What did human labelers prefer?
options: The giant base model over the fine-tuned models in every test
A model trained only on code over every dialogue model
Random outputs over any fine-tuned model for creativity
The small fine-tuned InstructGPT model over the base GPT-3, despite having far fewer parameters
questions.answer: The small fine-tuned InstructGPT model over the base GPT-3, despite having far fewer parameters
questions.explanation: Labelers preferred the small aligned model's answers to the giant base model's, the result that sold the field on alignment over raw scale. The code-only distractor is backwards: general helpfulness won, not a narrow specialty.

questions.text: The 2022 Constitutional AI paper trains a harmless assistant in two stages. What are they?
options: Pretraining on books, then deleting the safety filter
Training a chatbot, then replacing it with a search engine
Supervised learning from self-revisions, then reinforcement learning on AI-generated preference labels
Collecting user thumbs-downs, then banning those users
questions.answer: Supervised learning from self-revisions, then reinforcement learning on AI-generated preference labels
questions.explanation: First the model revises its own answers against the constitution and learns from those revisions, then a preference model trained on AI-labelled comparisons steers it with reinforcement learning. User thumbs-downs are the human-feedback loop this pipeline was designed to replace.

questions.text: Besides masked language modeling, BERT's original pretraining used a second objective on sentence pairs. What was it?
options: Translating each sentence into twelve new languages
Next-sentence prediction, deciding whether the second sentence follows the first
Counting how many nouns appear in each paragraph
Reconstructing whole documents from a single summary vector
questions.answer: Next-sentence prediction, deciding whether the second sentence follows the first
questions.explanation: BERT learned whether sentence B actually follows sentence A, which taught it relationships between sentences rather than just words inside them. Translation is the multilingual-BERT association people reach for, but it was never a pretraining objective.

questions.text: Why did OpenAI release GPT-2 in stages in 2019, starting with a small model?
options: Concerns about malicious uses such as disinformation, so larger versions followed months later
The larger models had failed every benchmark and were abandoned
A court order banned language models above a fixed size
The team had lost the training code and rebuilt it slowly
questions.answer: Concerns about malicious uses such as disinformation, so larger versions followed months later
questions.explanation: OpenAI cited misuse worries including disinformation and released progressively larger versions as the expected harms failed to materialize. Failed benchmarks would have killed the project, not staged it, which is why that distractor reverses the story.

questions.text: The 2016 AlphaGo Nature paper combined deep neural networks with Monte Carlo tree search. What did the neural networks first learn from?
options: Only games AlphaGo played against itself from random moves
Hand-coded Go proverbs written by game designers
A database of grandmaster chess openings
Millions of positions from human expert games, before reinforcement learning self-play refined them
questions.answer: Millions of positions from human expert games, before reinforcement learning self-play refined them
questions.explanation: The networks first imitated millions of human expert positions, then improved through self-play reinforcement learning, with tree search guiding both training and play. Pure self-play from scratch was the later AlphaGo Zero breakthrough, not the 2016 system.

questions.text: The 2021 DALL-E paper generated images from text with a two-stage recipe. What did it do?
options: Diffusing pure noise into pictures over hundreds of steps
Copying the closest training image for each prompt
Compressing images into discrete tokens, then training a transformer to predict them from text
Rendering 3D meshes with a physics engine, then photographing them
questions.answer: Compressing images into discrete tokens, then training a transformer to predict them from text
questions.explanation: A discrete autoencoder compresses each image to a grid of tokens, and the transformer learns to emit that grid conditioned on text, unifying vision and language as one sequence problem. Diffusion over noise is the rival family that later overtook this recipe for image quality.

questions.text: DeepMind's 2022 Flamingo paper gave a frozen language model visual understanding. How did images feed into the language model?
options: By converting every picture into a long English caption first
Through a Perceiver-style resampler whose visual tokens plug into gated cross-attention layers
By retraining the whole language model from scratch on pixels
Through a retrieval index that pastes in similar photos
questions.answer: Through a Perceiver-style resampler whose visual tokens plug into gated cross-attention layers
questions.explanation: A Perceiver-style resampler squeezes each image into a few visual tokens that enter the frozen language model through gated cross-attention, preserving its few-shot abilities. Retraining everything from scratch would destroy the language priors the whole trick relies on.

questions.text: Which researcher has earned the title "the Godfather of AI"?
questions.explanation: Hinton spent decades on neural networks while almost nobody else did, including through both of the field's winters, and then supervised the work that produced AlexNet in 2012. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield, and he has been blunt about the safety risks ever since.

questions.text: Which researcher built the ImageNet dataset and has been called the Godmother of AI?
questions.explanation: Li started building ImageNet in 2007 and it is hard to overstate what it did, because most of modern computer vision only became possible once the data existed. She has spent the last several years arguing that the bottleneck has moved from algorithms to data quality, and that the next ImageNet has not been built yet.

questions.text: In 2024, which AI researcher shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on protein structure prediction?
questions.explanation: In 2024 Hassabis and John Jumper shared half the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and David Baker took the other half for computational protein design. AlphaFold had already predicted the structure of over 200 million proteins by then, which is close to every protein catalogued by hand.

questions.text: Which researcher co-created AlexNet alongside Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton?
questions.explanation: Sutskever was a graduate student at Toronto at the time, and AlexNet is one of the most cited papers in the whole field. He went on to co-found OpenAI, lead the company that made the GPT models, and spend a decade convinced that scaling alone would get to something extraordinary.

questions.text: Which researcher founded DAIR, the Distributed AI Research Institute, and is known for work on algorithmic bias?
questions.explanation: Gebru co-founded Black in AI and led a research team at Google that was pushed out over a paper about the risks of large language models. DAIR came out of that, and the firing became the most public argument anyone in the field has had about what research is allowed to say out loud.

questions.text: Which scholar won the 1978 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences and is known for bounded rationality?
questions.explanation: Simon argued that people satisfice, they look for good enough rather than optimal, and he said the same thing about machines. He and Allen Newell built the Logic Theorist and GPS, and both of them are on the short list of anyone trying to explain where the idea of a thinking machine came from.

questions.text: Who has been the chief executive officer of OpenAI since 2019?
questions.explanation: Altman became CEO in 2019, a year after OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit research lab with the explicit goal of not pursuing profit. That structure has been rewritten twice since, and the board upheaval in November 2023 was the loudest argument anybody has had about who actually controls the company.

questions.text: Which English mathematician designed the Turing test and is regarded as the father of theoretical computer science?
questions.explanation: Turing formalized the idea of a general purpose computing machine and helped break the Enigma code at Bletchley Park. He proposed the imitation game in 1950, and six years later he wrote a paper on machine learning that is the reason the term exists at all.

questions.text: Which researcher was a cofounder and head of Google Brain, and later served as Chief Scientist at Baidu?
questions.explanation: Ng ran Google Brain when the company was largely still using speech and ads research, then spent three years at Baidu before leaving to work on education. He also co-founded Coursera and Deeplearning.ai, which is why his name shows up in far more machine learning course syllabuses than research papers.

questions.text: Which researcher co-founded Anthropic with his sister, and had previously been vice president of research at OpenAI?
questions.explanation: Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic in January 2021 with the stated goal of promoting AI safety, and he ran research at OpenAI first. Their publishing agenda, Constitutional AI in particular, has been the most sustained public attempt so far to write alignment research down instead of only doing it.

questions.text: Who founded the community blog LessWrong and co-founded the Machine Intelligence Research Institute?
questions.explanation: Yudkowsky founded LessWrong in 2009 using his own posts as seed material, and co-founded MIRI to work on friendly AI. Robin Hanson is the tempting miss because he co-wrote the predecessor blog Overcoming Bias, but he kept that blog while Yudkowsky launched LessWrong. Yudkowsky also spread rationalist ideas through the fanfiction novel Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality.

questions.text: Who wrote the 2014 book Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies?
questions.explanation: Bostrom, then at Oxford, published Superintelligence in 2014 and it became a New York Times bestseller that carried AI risk into the mainstream. Yudkowsky is the closest miss because his writing on intelligence explosion influenced the book, but he never wrote it. The paperclip maximizer thought experiment comes from Bostrom's work on the orthogonality thesis.

questions.text: Who developed convolutional neural networks in the 1980s and served as Meta chief AI scientist?
questions.explanation: LeCun invented convolutional networks at Bell Labs in the late 1980s, including the LeNet system for reading handwritten checks. Hinton is the tempting miss because he shared the 2018 Turing Award with LeCun and Bengio, but his fame rests on backpropagation and deep belief nets rather than CNNs. LeCun joined Facebook in 2013 to found FAIR and served as chief AI scientist for a decade.

questions.text: Who founded the Quebec AI institute Mila and shared the 2018 Turing Award with Hinton and LeCun?
questions.explanation: Bengio founded Mila, the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute in Montreal, and split the 2018 Turing Award for deep learning breakthroughs. Hassabis is the closest miss because he is another famous lab leader, but he co-founded DeepMind and won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry instead. Bengio also co-directs the CIFAR Learning in Machines and Brains program with LeCun.

questions.text: Who led Tesla Autopilot vision as director of AI and later became known for the Zero to Hero neural network videos?
questions.explanation: Karpathy, an OpenAI founding member, joined Tesla in 2017 and led the Autopilot vision team until 2022. George Hotz is the tempting miss because he also worked briefly with Musk on driving automation, but he founded comma.ai instead of leading Tesla AI. Karpathy returned to OpenAI in 2023 and later founded the AI education company Eureka Labs in 2024.

questions.text: Which OpenAI CTO became interim CEO immediately after Sam Altman was fired in November 2023?
questions.explanation: Murati, OpenAI CTO since 2022, stepped in as interim CEO on November 17 2023 when the board removed Altman. Emmett Shear is the tempting miss because he held the same interim title days later, but he came from Twitch and was second in the sequence. Murati left OpenAI in September 2024 and founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025.

questions.text: Who co-founded Mistral AI in 2023 and serves as its CEO after working at DeepMind Paris?
questions.explanation: Mensch left DeepMind Paris in May 2023 and co-founded Mistral AI with Guillaume Lample and Timothee Lacroix, becoming CEO. Lample is the tempting miss because he is also a Mistral co-founder, but he serves as chief scientist rather than CEO. Under Mensch, Mistral released open-weight models like Mistral 7B and Mixtral and became the flagship of European AI.

questions.text: Who founded the Chinese AI company DeepSeek after building the High-Flyer quantitative hedge fund?
questions.explanation: Liang co-founded the quant fund High-Flyer in 2015 and launched DeepSeek in 2023, funding it from the fund and stockpiling Nvidia chips before export controls. Kai-Fu Lee is the tempting miss because he is the other famous Chinese AI founder-investor, but his company is 01.AI rather than DeepSeek. DeepSeek stunned markets in early 2025 when its R1 reasoning model matched Western rivals at far lower reported cost.

questions.text: Who co-founded DeepMind and Inflection AI and became CEO of Microsoft AI in 2024?
questions.explanation: Suleyman co-founded DeepMind in 2010, left Google in 2022 to co-found Inflection AI, then joined Microsoft in March 2024 to lead Copilot and consumer AI. Shane Legg is the tempting miss because he is the third DeepMind co-founder, but he stayed in research rather than taking the Microsoft role. Suleyman also wrote the 2023 book The Coming Wave about AI risk.

questions.text: Which Transformer co-author left Google to found Character.AI and returned to Google in 2024?
questions.explanation: Shazeer, a Google researcher since 2000 who designed key parts of the Transformer, left in 2021 with Daniel De Freitas to found Character.AI. Llion Jones is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author who left Google for a startup, but he joined Sakana AI in Tokyo rather than founding Character.AI. Google brought Shazeer back in August 2024 with a licensing deal reported at over 2 billion dollars.

questions.text: Which Transformer paper co-author went on to co-found and lead Cohere as CEO?
questions.explanation: Gomez was a 20-year-old intern at Google Brain when he co-authored Attention Is All You Need in 2017, then co-founded Cohere in 2019 as CEO. Illia Polosukhin is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author turned founder, but he founded NEAR Protocol rather than Cohere. Cohere focuses on enterprise AI models rather than consumer chatbots.

questions.text: Who succeeded Mira Murati as OpenAI interim CEO during the November 2023 leadership crisis?
questions.explanation: Shear, who co-founded Justin.tv and led Twitch as CEO until 2023, accepted the interim job on November 20 after Murati and left when Altman was reinstated days later. Bret Taylor is the tempting miss because he became board chair in the shake-up, but he never held the CEO title. Shear had publicly estimated a 5 to 50 percent chance of AI-caused doom, which drew attention during his brief tenure.

questions.text: Which leather-jacketed executive has led Nvidia as CEO since co-founding it in 1993?
questions.explanation: Huang founded Nvidia with two Sun colleagues and never left, riding gaming graphics into the AI boom in his trademark leather jacket. Morris Chang is the tempting miss because TSMC fabs Nvidia's chips, but he never ran Nvidia.

questions.text: Who became CEO of AMD in 2014 and led its turnaround?
questions.explanation: Su bet AMD on Zen and high-performance chiplets, taking it from near-bankruptcy to datacenter contender. Rory Read is the tempting miss because he was her immediate predecessor as CEO, but the turnaround belongs to Su.

questions.text: Who became CEO of Microsoft in 2014 and backed OpenAI with billions?
questions.explanation: Nadella pivoted Microsoft to cloud-first and placed the $1 billion 2019 bet on OpenAI that grew into the defining AI partnership. Steve Ballmer is the tempting miss because he was the previous CEO, but the OpenAI deal is Nadella's era.

questions.text: Which OpenAI co-founder left the lab and founded xAI in 2023?
questions.explanation: Musk co-founded OpenAI in 2015, departed in 2018, and launched xAI with its Grok chatbot in 2023. Sam Altman is the tempting miss because he is the famous OpenAI face, but he stayed as CEO while Musk left and competed.

questions.text: Before co-founding Google Brain, Jeff Dean had already helped build which Google system for processing data at a scale nobody had attempted?
questions.explanation: MapReduce, with Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat, is the distributed computation technique that let Google index the web by splitting work across thousands of machines. He then co-founded Google Brain in 2011 and became Google's chief scientist, so he shows up twice in AI history for two unrelated reasons.

questions.text: Who is the first author of the 2015 ResNet paper on deep residual learning?
questions.explanation: He led the Microsoft Research Asia team whose skip connections let networks train hundreds of layers deep. Xiangyu Zhang is the tempting miss because he is the second author, but the paper opens with He, Zhang, Ren and Sun in that order.

questions.text: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993, and the meetings where the business plan was written happened in a roadside diner in East San Jose. Which restaurant chain was it?
questions.explanation: Huang washed dishes and waited tables at a Denny's through his teens in Oregon, so when he needed somewhere quiet with cheap coffee for the 1992 planning meetings he picked the same chain, and Nvidia was founded from a breakfast booth. The company's first capital was $600, split three ways out of the founders' pockets.

questions.text: Lisa Su led AMD's largest-ever purchase, announced in 2020 and completed in February 2022, to bring programmable logic into the chip lineup. Which company did AMD buy?
questions.explanation: Xilinx built the first commercially viable FPGA, and buying it gave AMD the programmable logic behind the adaptive-computing parts it now sells against Nvidia. Altera is the tempting miss because it was the other FPGA pioneer, but that company ended up inside Intel, and the Arm deal that collapsed in 2022 was Nvidia's, not AMD's.

questions.text: Microsoft's AI bet began with a $1 billion investment in 2019, and the total has since passed $13 billion. Which company has taken the money?
questions.explanation: Nadella arrived in 2014 after a decade of mobile bets that had not worked, then put $1 billion into OpenAI in 2019 in exchange for Azure becoming the required home for OpenAI's models. That partnership became the engine behind Copilot. Anthropic is the tempting miss because it is the other lab with giant corporate backers, but those are Amazon and Google.

questions.text: Meta bought a 49% stake in Scale AI for more than $14 billion in 2025 and hired the company's founder to run Meta Superintelligence Labs as its Chief AI Officer. Who is he?
questions.explanation: Wang left MIT at 19 to build Scale AI, turning data labelling and model evaluation into the business every frontier lab buys from, and the stake Meta bought cost roughly $14.3 billion and valued the company at about $29 billion. Nat Friedman is the tempting miss because he arrived in the same shake-up, but he ran GitHub and took the product job, not the AI one.

questions.text: Hassabis turned DeepMind's protein work into a separate Alphabet company that uses AlphaFold to hunt for drug targets. What is that company called?
questions.explanation: Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in London in 2010 and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with John Jumper for protein structure prediction. Isomorphic Labs was announced in November 2021 as a DeepMind spin-off that reuses AlphaFold to find drug targets, and he runs it as CEO while also leading Google DeepMind as its CEO. Recursion is the tempting miss because it is a well-known AI drug-discovery company, but it grew out of a different lineage.

questions.text: Which researcher behind AlphaFold was named one of Nature's ten 'people who mattered' in science in 2021?
questions.explanation: Jumper was the first author of the AlphaFold 2 paper Nature published in July 2021, and he shared half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. David Baker is the tempting miss because he took the other half of that prize, for computational protein design, but his work was designing proteins rather than predicting their shapes.

questions.text: The image generator that spent its 2022 open beta inside Discord is run by a founder who had previously co-founded Leap Motion, the gesture-control hardware company. Who is he?
questions.explanation: Holz founded Midjourney in San Francisco, and by the August 2022 open beta he told The Register the company was already profitable, which was unusual for a generative-image startup. Jason Allen is the tempting miss because his AI-generated entry won the digital art prize at the 2022 Colorado State Fair, but Allen wrote the prompt and entered the work rather than building the tool.

questions.text: Hugging Face began in New York in 2016 as a chatbot for teenagers and took its name from a hugging-face emoji. Two of its three French co-founders are Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. Who is the third?
questions.explanation: The company open-sourced the model behind its chatbot and pivoted into a hub where anyone can publish and download models, which is why most open weights now live there. Emad Mostaque is the tempting miss because he ran the competing Stable Diffusion company, which went the other way and open-sourced everything it made.

questions.text: After Tesla, Andrej Karpathy stopped trying to build the biggest models and in 2024 started a company to teach people how they work. Which AI education company did he found?
questions.explanation: Karpathy's public rebuilds of a language model from scratch, most famously the nanoGPT repository, made him the field's default teacher for how a model is actually trained. Deeplearning.ai is the tempting miss because it is the other famous name in AI courses, but that is Andrew Ng's company, and fast.ai belongs to Jeremy Howard.

questions.text: Which researcher, a co-author of the 2018 Gender Shades audit that found facial-analysis systems perform worst on dark-skinned women, founded the Algorithmic Justice League?
questions.explanation: Buolamwini and Gebru's audit tested commercial systems that police departments were buying, which is what pushed facial-recognition bias into the mainstream. Gebru is the tempting miss because she co-wrote that paper and later founded DAIR after being pushed out of Google, but the Algorithmic Justice League is Buolamwini's, and she frames the problem as an artist as much as a researcher.

questions.text: Which CEO personally delivered the first Nvidia DGX-1 supercomputer to OpenAI in August 2016?
questions.explanation: Huang showed up at OpenAI's office in 2016 with the first DGX-1, built for deep learning, and Elon Musk posted the photo of the handover. Lisa Su is the tempting miss because she runs AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, but in 2016 she had only just started AMD's turnaround and had no DGX to deliver.

questions.text: Lisa Su, who became AMD CEO in 2014, is reported to be what to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang?
questions.explanation: Multiple profiles report Su and Huang are relatives through Taiwanese families: Su's mother and Huang are first cousins, so Su and Huang are first cousins once removed. His sister is the tempting miss because the family link is real, but the reported relationship is a cousin link, not a sibling one.

questions.text: Which Microsoft CEO published the memoir Hit Refresh in 2017 about transforming the company?
questions.explanation: Nadella wrote Hit Refresh in 2017, three years after succeeding Ballmer, describing the shift to cloud and empathy in leadership. Ballmer is the tempting miss because he was CEO just before, but he left in 2014 and never wrote about the cloud turnaround.

questions.text: Which company grew out of the online bank X.com that Elon Musk co-founded in 1999?
questions.explanation: Musk founded X.com in 1999, it merged with Confinity in 2000 and was renamed PayPal in 2001 before eBay bought it. Tesla is the tempting miss because Musk is its public face, but he joined Tesla in 2004 as an investor, long after X.com became PayPal.

questions.text: Who co-founded Facebook in a Harvard dorm room in 2004?
questions.explanation: Zuckerberg launched thefacebook.com in February 2004 with Dustin Moskovitz, Eduardo Saverin and others before dropping out. Jack Dorsey is the tempting miss because he founded another social network, but his was Twitter in 2006, not Facebook.

questions.text: Who led the DeepMind team behind AlphaGo's 2016 victory over Lee Sedol?
questions.explanation: Silver led the reinforcement learning work behind AlphaGo and later AlphaZero, combining search with deep networks trained by self-play. Hassabis is the tempting miss because he co-founded DeepMind and was the public face of the match, but the AlphaGo papers list Silver as the lead researcher.

questions.text: Who was the first author of OpenAI's 2021 CLIP paper on learning vision from language?
questions.explanation: Radford led CLIP, which trained on 400 million image-text pairs and enabled zero-shot image classification without labeled data. Sutskever is the tempting miss because he led much of OpenAI's early research, but by 2021 he was focused on alignment and was not on the CLIP author list.

questions.text: Who created the Keras deep-learning library in 2015 while working at Google?
questions.explanation: Chollet released Keras in 2015 as a friendly front end for neural nets, and it later became the high-level API inside TensorFlow. Howard is the tempting miss because he built fast.ai on top of similar ideas, but his library came later and was aimed at courses, not as a TensorFlow API.

questions.text: Who co-founded fast.ai with Rachel Thomas in 2016 to make deep learning accessible?
questions.explanation: Howard and Thomas launched fast.ai in 2016 with free courses and software that put practical training ahead of theory. Ng is the tempting miss because his Coursera courses taught millions, but his platform was Deeplearning.ai, not fast.ai.

questions.text: Who was the first author of OpenAI's 2020 Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models paper?
questions.explanation: Kaplan's 2020 paper showed loss falls predictably with model size, data and compute, which set off the race to scale. Amodei is the tempting miss because he was a senior author and later cited the laws when founding Anthropic, but Kaplan led the analysis.

source.label: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models on arXiv

questions.text: Which Anthropic researcher led early work on model character and the 2022 Constitutional AI approach?
questions.explanation: Askell drove Anthropic's work on shaping Claude's character and co-authored the Constitutional AI paper that replaced some human feedback with AI feedback. Leike is the tempting miss because he later led superalignment work, but in 2022 he was still at OpenAI, not on the Constitutional AI team.

questions.text: Who co-led OpenAI's Superalignment team with Ilya Sutskever in 2023 and resigned in May 2024 to join Anthropic?
questions.explanation: Leike ran Superalignment with Sutskever to study how to control future superintelligent systems, then left saying he disagreed with OpenAI's priorities. Schulman is the tempting miss because he was another senior alignment researcher who later moved to Anthropic, but he never led Superalignment.

questions.text: Which OpenAI co-founder led post-training for ChatGPT and left OpenAI in August 2024 for Anthropic?
questions.explanation: Schulman co-founded OpenAI in 2015 and ran the reinforcement learning work that turned GPT into ChatGPT. Brockman is the tempting miss because he is the other co-founder who stayed visible as president, but he never led ChatGPT post-training and did not leave for Anthropic.

questions.text: Which OpenAI president and co-founder had previously been CTO of Stripe?
questions.explanation: Brockman joined Stripe as CTO in 2013, then left to co-found OpenAI in 2015 and run its engineering as president. Altman is the tempting miss because he is the public CEO, but he came from Y Combinator, not Stripe.

questions.text: Who co-founded the Future of Life Institute in 2014 and wrote Life 3.0 in 2017?
questions.explanation: Tegmark, an MIT cosmologist, started FLI with Jaan Tallinn and wrote Life 3.0 about stages of life with AI. Bostrom is the tempting miss because his 2014 book Superintelligence defined the same debate, but he never founded FLI.

questions.text: Which Skype co-founder co-founded the Future of Life Institute and Cambridge's Centre for the Study of Existential Risk?
questions.explanation: Tallinn helped build Skype, then used the proceeds to fund FLI in 2014 and CSER with Huw Price and others. Zennstrom is the tempting miss because he was the better-known Skype co-founder, but the safety institutes were Tallinn's project.

questions.text: Which researcher, with Andrew Barto, won the 2024 Turing Award for reinforcement learning?
questions.explanation: Sutton and Barto wrote Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction in 1998 and shared the 2024 Turing Award for the field. Barto is the tempting miss because he shares the prize and the book, but the question asks for his co-author, and Silver was their intellectual successor at DeepMind, not the co-winner.

questions.text: Who won the 2011 Turing Award for work on Bayesian networks and causal reasoning?
questions.explanation: Pearl's work on probabilistic reasoning and do-calculus gave AI a formal language for cause and effect, recognized by the 2011 Turing Award. Hinton is the tempting miss because he later won the same prize in 2018 for deep learning, but his award was seven years after Pearl's.

questions.text: Who co-authored the 1969 book Perceptrons with Seymour Papert?
questions.explanation: Minsky and Papert's 1969 book showed limits of single-layer perceptrons, which helped freeze neural-net funding for a decade. McCarthy is the tempting miss because he co-organized Dartmouth with Minsky, but Perceptrons was Minsky and Papert's critique, not his.

questions.text: Who founded Stability AI in 2019 and released Stable Diffusion in 2022?
questions.explanation: Mostaque founded Stability AI in London in 2019 and funded the Stable Diffusion release that made open image models mainstream in 2022. Holz is the tempting miss because he founded Midjourney the same year image models broke out, but his tool stayed closed while Stability open-sourced its weights.

questions.text: Which Runway co-founder has served as its CEO since its founding in 2018?
questions.explanation: Valenzuela co-founded Runway in New York in 2018 with Germanidis and Matamala and stayed as CEO through the Gen-2 video push. Germanidis is the tempting miss because he is also a co-founder, but he serves in a research role rather than as CEO.

questions.text: Which artist won the 2022 Colorado State Fair digital-art prize with the Midjourney work Theatre d'Opera Spatial?
questions.explanation: Allen entered the Midjourney image in 2022 and the win sparked the first mainstream debate over whether AI art counts as art. Eldagsen is the tempting miss because he also made headlines for AI art in 2023, but he refused the Sony prize rather than winning in Colorado.

questions.text: Which 2023 viral track used AI-cloned voices of Drake and The Weeknd and was pulled from streaming?
questions.explanation: The anonymous ghostwriter released Heart on My Sleeve in April 2023 with cloned Drake and Weeknd vocals, and labels had it removed within days. Taylor Made Freestyle is the tempting miss because Drake himself used AI Tupac and Snoop voices on it in 2024, but that was an official diss track, not the 2023 clone stunt. Grimes responded by offering 50 percent royalties to anyone cloning her voice.

source.title: Heart on My Sleeve (Ghostwriter977 song)
source.label: Heart on My Sleeve (Ghostwriter977 song) on Wikipedia

questions.text: Which former MIT researcher has hosted the Lex Fridman Podcast since 2018 with long interviews of AI scientists?
questions.explanation: Fridman, who worked on autonomous vehicles at MIT, started the podcast in 2018 and became the default long-form interviewer for AI leaders. Dwarkesh Patel is the tempting miss because he also interviews the same researchers at length, but his show started later and grew out of his blog, not MIT research.

questions.text: Who became president of the Signal Foundation in 2022 after researching AI and labor?
questions.explanation: Whittaker organized against Project Maven at Google, then took over Signal in 2022 to run private messaging at scale. Crawford is the tempting miss because she wrote Atlas of AI in 2021 about the same extractive costs, but she stayed in research rather than running Signal.

questions.text: Who founded the Chinese AI startup 01.AI in 2023 after leading Google China?
questions.explanation: Lee ran Google China and later Sinovation Ventures before founding 01.AI in 2023 to build open Chinese language models. Liang Wenfeng is the tempting miss because he founded the other famous Chinese open-weights lab, but his company is DeepSeek, not 01.AI.

questions.text: Who founded TSMC in Taiwan in 1987 and pioneered the foundry model of making chips for others?
questions.explanation: Chang founded TSMC in 1987 after decades at Texas Instruments, betting that design and manufacturing should split. Huang is the tempting miss because Nvidia is TSMC's most famous customer, but he buys wafers from Chang's company rather than founding it.

questions.text: Which chip architect led development of AMD's Zen, Apple's A4 and A5, and Tesla's self-driving chip?
questions.explanation: Keller led AMD's K8 and later Zen teams, did two stints at Apple on the A4 and A5, then ran Tesla Autopilot hardware before moving to Intel and Tenstorrent. Faggin is the tempting miss because he designed the Intel 4004, but his landmark work was fifty years before Keller's Zen comeback.

questions.text: Who was the first PhD student of AI researcher Andrew Ng?
questions.explanation: Abbeel earned his PhD at Stanford under Andrew Ng, who was then a first-year professor, and later became a Berkeley professor and co-founded Covariant. Fei-Fei Li is the tempting miss because she is also a Stanford AI professor who worked with Ng, but she was not his first doctoral student.

questions.text: Which UC Berkeley professor developed guided policy search for robotic control?
questions.explanation: Levine, a Berkeley professor, developed guided policy search to train deep networks for complex robotic tasks. Abbeel is the tempting miss because he advised Levine's postdoc and also works on robot learning, but guided policy search is Levine's contribution.

questions.text: Which researcher introduced Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) in 2017?
questions.explanation: Finn and colleagues at Berkeley introduced MAML, which trains models to adapt quickly to new tasks with few examples. Abbeel is the tempting miss as a co-author and her doctoral advisor, but Finn led the work.

questions.text: Which Stanford professor founded the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM)?
questions.explanation: Liang founded CRFM at Stanford to study the development and evaluation of foundation models. Fei-Fei Li is the tempting miss as a famous Stanford AI professor, but CRFM is Liang's initiative.

questions.text: Which Stanford computer scientist won a MacArthur 'genius' grant in 2015?
questions.explanation: Ré won the MacArthur Fellowship in 2015 for work on big data analysis and co-founded Lattice.io, later acquired by Apple. Liang is the tempting miss as another Stanford professor, but the MacArthur went to Ré.

questions.text: Who created the Apache Spark data processing engine?
questions.explanation: Zaharia created Apache Spark while at UC Berkeley as a faster alternative to MapReduce. Stoica is the tempting miss because he co-founded Databricks with Zaharia, but Spark itself was Zaharia's project.

questions.text: Which UC Berkeley professor co-founded Anyscale, the company behind the Ray framework?
questions.explanation: Stoica co-founded Anyscale with the original developers of Ray. Zaharia is the tempting miss because he also co-founded Databricks with Stoica, but Anyscale and Ray are Stoica's venture.

questions.text: Who created the Python programming language?
questions.explanation: Van Rossum created Python in 1989 as a hobby project over Christmas. Oliphant is the tempting miss because he created NumPy, a core Python library, but not the language itself.

questions.text: GitHub Copilot was first announced on what date?
questions.explanation: It is a code completion assistant for Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Neovim, Eclipse and the JetBrains IDEs, built by GitHub with OpenAI. It shipped two years before ChatGPT, which makes it a useful reminder that coding assistants were quietly the first mainstream AI product.

questions.text: Runway AI is a New York company best known for which product category?
questions.explanation: Video, images and other multimedia, through commercial text to video and video generative models. It is one of a cluster of companies, along with Stability AI and Midjourney, that turned generative research into tools filmmakers and designers actually pay for.

questions.text: ElevenLabs, founded in 2022, specialises in which area of AI?
questions.explanation: Speech, and it was founded by Piotr Dąbkowski and Mateusz Staniszewski, who both worked on speech at Google. The company is based in London with offices in New York, Warsaw and San Francisco, which is an unusual arrangement for a company founded by two Polish entrepreneurs and incorporated in the US.

questions.text: Sora, previewed by OpenAI in February 2024, became generally available to which users first?
questions.explanation: Sora generates text to video, and it reached paying ChatGPT subscribers before it reached anyone else. The rollout was staggered by tier and then by region through 2024, which is why a model previewed in February was still gated months later.

questions.text: Google's NotebookLM was renamed in 2025. What is it now called?
questions.explanation: Gemini Notebook, with LM standing for Language Model, and it is a retrieval augmented research and note taking tool. It answers only from documents you give it and cites them, which is the product form that RAG actually looks like when it is aimed at people rather than engineers.

questions.text: What does the LM in the name NotebookLM stand for?
questions.explanation: Language Model, which is the only technical term in the product name. The rest of the name describes what the tool does, which is reading your notes back to you with citations, and the abbreviation is a small joke aimed at people who would recognise it.

questions.text: Which startup launched the screenless AI Pin wearable that flopped in 2024?
questions.explanation: Humane, founded by ex-Apple staffers, shipped the screenless AI Pin in 2024 to dismal reviews over heat, battery and hallucinations. Rabbit is the tempting miss because its R1 flopped the same year, but the pin was Humane's. HP bought most of the company in early 2025 and shut the device down.

questions.text: Which device unveiled at CES in January 2024 promised a large action model that operates apps for you?
questions.explanation: Rabbit unveiled the 199-dollar R1 at CES in January 2024, promising a large action model that clicks through apps for you. The Apple Vision Pro is the tempting miss as the other hyped early-2024 gadget, but the action-model pitch was Rabbit's. Reviewers found a half-baked assistant and called it barely reviewable.

questions.text: Which image service runs through Discord after entering open beta in July 2022?
questions.explanation: Midjourney entered open beta in July 2022 as a bot living entirely inside Discord. Stable Diffusion is the tempting miss because it also arrived that summer, but it runs anywhere while Midjourney stayed Discord-only. Founder David Holz had previously built the Leap Motion controller.

questions.text: Which NotebookLM feature that turns documents into podcast-style chats went viral in September 2024?
questions.explanation: NotebookLM's Audio Overviews, which turn uploaded documents into a two-host podcast chat, went viral in September 2024. Mind Maps is the tempting miss as another NotebookLM view, but the 2024 sensation was audio. Fans shared clips of synthetic hosts bantering over meeting notes and syllabi.

questions.text: Which label had the AI track Heart on My Sleeve pulled from streaming in April 2023?
questions.explanation: The April 2023 track Heart on My Sleeve used AI-cloned vocals of Drake and The Weeknd, and Universal Music Group had it pulled from streaming. Sony Music is the tempting miss as another major label, but UMG acted because both mimicked artists sit on its roster. The anonymous maker ghostwriter still submitted the track for Grammy consideration.

source.title: Heart on My Sleeve (Ghostwriter song)
source.label: Heart on My Sleeve (Ghostwriter song) on Wikipedia

questions.text: How many users did ChatGPT gain in its first two months after launching in November 2022?
questions.explanation: ChatGPT reached about 100 million users within two months of its November 2022 launch, the fastest consumer ramp on record then. Fifty million is the tempting undercount, but outside trackers put the two-month figure at 100 million. UBS analysts called it the fastest-growing consumer app in history.

questions.text: Meta began rolling out a product called Muse to US users on September 8, 2026. What kind of product is it?
options: A personal AI agent you message that works on your apps for you
A multimodal model that generates images and video inside Meta apps
A paid subscription that bundles Meta AI with your Instagram account
A pair of smart glasses with a camera and a built-in voice assistant
questions.answer: A personal AI agent you message that works on your apps for you
questions.explanation: Muse is Meta's personal agent: you tell it what needs doing and it opens a browser, fills in forms, buys things, and comes back to ask before it sends an email or spends money. It runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated virtual machine holding both the agent and your data, and you reach it in the Muse app or straight in WhatsApp. The name is deliberately shared with Meta's model line, because Muse runs on Muse Spark, which Meta calls its most capable model to date.

questions.text: Suno launched its v6 music models on September 9, 2026, the first generation it built with music industry partners. Which partners did Suno name?
options: Universal Music Group, Sony Music and Believe
Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe
Warner Music Group, UMG and BMG
questions.answer: Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe
questions.explanation: Suno's own announcement names Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe as the partners v6 was developed with, and says the earlier models would be retired as v6 rolls out. Universal Music Group and Sony are the tempting miss because a player who remembers Suno's copyright fights reaches for the biggest labels rather than the ones that actually signed. The release also came as a set of three models: v6 and v6-wild for paid subscribers, and v6-mini free for everyone.
answerAliases: Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe

questions.text: Manus shipped Manus 2.0 and a separate agent app called Cue on September 28, 2026. In Cue, what does every agent get for itself?
options: A clone of your voice and your writing style
A dedicated GPU and a private server to run on
Its own social media accounts and login details
Its own email, phone number, wallet and computer
questions.answer: Its own email, phone number, wallet and computer
questions.explanation: Cue is a standalone app for personal agents, and Manus gives each one its own email, phone number, wallet and computer so it can message people, pay inside a budget you set, and finish a task on its own machine. A dedicated GPU and a private server is the tempting miss because Manus does sell a Cloud Computer, but that is a separate product you buy for a project. Several agents can also share a group chat and hand work to each other.
answerAliases: its own email, phone number, wallet and computer

questions.text: ByteDance launched Seedance 2.5 on July 31, 2026. Which two of ByteDance's own products did it roll out to on day one?
options: Doubao and Lark, with the API to follow
questions.explanation: Seedance 2.5 went live inside Jimeng AI, ByteDance's video creation app, and Doubao Pro, its paid assistant tier, with API access on BytePlus ModelArk promised for later. CapCut and TikTok are the tempting miss as the two ByteDance apps everyone knows, and Volcengine and ModelArk are the trap because the API only arrived after the consumer launch. The version jump hides the real change: single-pass length doubled from 15 seconds to 30.

questions.text: Black Forest Labs announced FLUX 3 in July 2026, its first model that generates video, and extended the same backbone to predict what a robot should do next. Which carmaker's production network is already testing that action model?
questions.explanation: The action half is called FLUX 3 Action and was built with mimic robotics, whose robots Black Forest Labs says have been tested and deployed at Audi. BFL is the Freiburg startup behind Stable Diffusion and the FLUX image models, and FLUX 3 is the first time it has shipped video at all. Audi's production lab framed the work as solving flexible, soft-body handling that conventionally programmed robot cells cannot handle economically.

source.label: Black Forest Labs on FLUX 3 and mimic robotics

questions.text: Dazzle, the startup founded by Marissa Mayer, launched its first product on September 29, 2026. Unlike most personal assistants, what does Dazzle use to work out who you are?
options: The email and calendar on your work account
The accounts you follow on social media
The voice memos and transcripts on your phone
The photos and screenshots in your camera roll
questions.answer: The photos and screenshots in your camera roll
questions.explanation: Dazzle's launch post is called Pictures, Not Prompts: the camera roll is the context layer, so a photo of a flat tyre becomes a booked repair and a school flyer becomes a calendar entry. Email and calendar is the tempting miss because that is where most personal assistants start, and Mayer's own post argues it skews them toward work. The post opened by noting that around five billion photos would be taken on smartphones that day.

source.label: Dazzle's launch post, Announcing Dazzle: Pictures, Not Prompts

questions.text: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS on September 23, 2026, and put each one into a different Google product on day one. The cheaper, high-volume model landed in which product?
questions.explanation: Flash-Lite is the throughput model, built for high-volume dubbing and expressive voice agents at scale, so it is the one Google put into Google Vids, its video creation tool. The creative-direction model, plain Flash, is the one that went into Gemini Notebook instead. Google AI Studio is the tempting miss because it is the other no-code surface, but it is a developer tool: you need an API key to use it.

questions.text: Sonos introduced Sonos 27, the next version of its audio operating system, in September 2026, and previewed its first in-house voice assistant alongside it. What was that in-house assistant built to do?
options: Answer general questions the way Alexa does today
Transcribe and translate speech in real time
Curate music and mood rather than general tasks
Read messages and manage your calendar for you
questions.answer: Curate music and mood rather than general tasks
questions.explanation: Sonos 27voice is deliberately narrow: Sonos describes its own first assistant as built for music and mood curation, not for handling general requests. The general-question distractor is the tempting miss because a speaker that answers questions is what most people picture, and the same release took the opposite route for everything else, adding Sonos 27mcp so an outside assistant such as OpenAI's ChatGPT could drive the system instead. The announcement also folded the Beam Ultra soundbar and Ace Ultra headphones into the portfolio.

questions.text: JetBrains took its AI coding agent Junie out of beta in June 2026. Which protocol did it rebuild the agent's IDE integration on for the general release?
questions.explanation: Junie's general release talks to the IDE over ACP, the same protocol Junie CLI already used, so one agent engine sits behind the AI chat, the Junie tool window and the terminal. Model Context Protocol is the tempting miss because it is the other big agent protocol of 2026, but MCP is about handing a model tools, not plugging an agent into an editor. Language Server Protocol is about completions and navigation.

questions.text: Cursor's Composer 2 and Composer 2.5 coding models were not trained from scratch: Cursor took an open base model from another lab and did its own continued pretraining and reinforcement learning on top. Which lab's open model was that base?
questions.explanation: Both Composer 2 and Composer 2.5 were built on Moonshot AI's open Kimi K2.5 checkpoint, a 1T parameter model that Cursor continued-pretrained on code and then reinforced on long-horizon tasks. The course change came in May 2026, when Cursor said it was training a significantly larger model from scratch with SpaceXAI, using ten times the total compute on Colossus 2. Alibaba and DeepSeek are the tempting misses because both ship strong open coding bases of their own.

questions.text: ChatGPT is developed and operated by which company?
questions.explanation: ChatGPT is OpenAI's generative AI chatbot, offered on a freemium model. Anthropic is the tempting miss because it is the other major independent lab, but it builds Claude.

questions.text: In June 2024 Anthropic added a Claude feature that generates and previews code and documents in a side panel. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Artifacts arrived with Claude 3.5 Sonnet in June 2024 and renders generated code, SVGs and documents in a separate window. Canvas is the tempting miss as a similar side-panel feature from another vendor.

questions.text: From the start, Google described Gemini as what kind of model?
questions.explanation: Gemini was designed to be multimodal from the outset, processing text, images, audio, video and code. Text-only is the tempting miss as the default for older large language models.

questions.text: GitHub Copilot is powered by OpenAI's Codex model, which descends from which GPT model?
questions.explanation: Codex is a descendant of GPT-3 fine-tuned on code. GPT-4 is the tempting miss as the newer model, but Codex's lineage traces to GPT-3.

questions.text: GitHub Copilot became generally available to the public in which year?
questions.explanation: Copilot was announced in June 2021 and reached general availability in 2022. 2021 is the tempting miss because that is when the technical preview began.

questions.text: Midjourney was founded by David Holz, who previously co-founded which company?
questions.explanation: David Holz co-founded Leap Motion, the hand-tracking controller company, before starting Midjourney. Oculus is the tempting miss as another VR-era hardware startup.

questions.text: Midjourney's original interface ran entirely through which platform?
questions.explanation: Midjourney launched as a Discord bot in 2022 and stayed Discord-first. A web app is the tempting miss as the interface most image tools use, but Midjourney's early identity was its Discord bot.

questions.text: OpenAI previewed Sora in which month of 2024?
questions.explanation: OpenAI previewed Sora in February 2024. June is the tempting miss as the month of many AI launches, but Sora's preview came earlier.

questions.text: NotebookLM's Audio Overviews simulate what format?
questions.explanation: Audio Overviews turn uploaded documents into a two-host podcast chat. A lecture is the tempting miss as another spoken format, but the viral 2024 feature was the podcast-style banter.

questions.text: NotebookLM answers questions based only on what?
questions.explanation: NotebookLM is grounded in the documents you give it and cites them. The open web is the tempting miss because most chatbots answer from training data or search, but NotebookLM stays inside your sources.

questions.text: In 2024 Google's AI Overviews suggested adding what to pizza sauce to keep cheese from sliding off?
questions.explanation: AI Overviews told users to add glue to pizza sauce, a hallucination drawn from a satirical Reddit comment. Cornstarch is the tempting miss as a real cooking thickener.

questions.text: Google rebranded Search Generative Experience as AI Overviews at which event in May 2024?
questions.explanation: AI Overviews were announced at Google I/O 2024. WWDC is the tempting miss as Apple's annual developer event.

questions.text: Perplexity AI is best described as what?
questions.explanation: Perplexity is a search engine that synthesizes answers and cites sources. An image generator is the tempting miss as the other common consumer AI product shape.

questions.text: What feature did Perplexity's answers include that early chatbots often lacked?
questions.explanation: Perplexity cites the sources it used to generate each answer. Code execution is the tempting miss as a feature many assistants later added.

questions.text: Character.ai lets users converse with what?
questions.explanation: Character.ai lets users chat with customizable characters, many based on fictional or real people. Only their own documents is the tempting miss as the NotebookLM model, not Character.ai.

questions.text: Poe is a chatbot aggregator launched by which company?
questions.explanation: Poe is Quora's platform for chatting with many large language models. Reddit is the tempting miss as another Q&A community, but Poe came from Quora.

questions.text: Grok is integrated into which social platform?
questions.explanation: Grok is integrated into the X social network. Reddit is the tempting miss as another large discussion platform.

questions.text: Rabbit's R1 promised a 'large action model' (LAM). What was a LAM meant to do?
options: Operate apps and interfaces for you
questions.answer: Operate apps and interfaces for you
questions.explanation: A LAM was meant to click through apps and interfaces on the user's behalf. Generate music is the tempting miss as another generative AI capability.

questions.text: After poor reviews, most of Humane was acquired by which company in early 2025?
questions.explanation: HP bought most of Humane in early 2025 and shut down the AI Pin. Apple is the tempting miss because Humane's founders were ex-Apple.

questions.text: In 2024 a DPD chatbot was taken offline after doing what?
questions.explanation: DPD's chatbot was coaxed into swearing and writing a poem calling the company useless. Leaking passwords is the tempting miss as a more dramatic chatbot failure, but the real incident was the abuse.

questions.text: In 2023 a Chevrolet dealership's AI chatbot agreed to sell a new Tahoe for how much?
questions.explanation: A dealership's ChatGPT-powered bot agreed to sell a Tahoe for one dollar after a user prompted it. Free is the tempting miss as an even more absurd outcome, but the reported figure was $1.

questions.text: Cursor is an AI-first code editor built as a fork of which editor?
questions.explanation: Cursor is built on top of VS Code. JetBrains is the tempting miss as another major IDE family, but Cursor forked VS Code.

questions.text: Windsurf, an AI code editor, was originally known under what name?
questions.explanation: Windsurf started life as Codeium before rebranding. Copilot is the tempting miss as the Microsoft product it competes with.

questions.text: Suno is an AI product for generating what?
questions.explanation: Suno generates full songs from text prompts. Images is the tempting miss as the other popular generative medium.

questions.text: Udio is a competitor to Suno in which category?
questions.explanation: Udio, like Suno, generates music from prompts. Image generation is the tempting miss as the other crowded generative space.

questions.text: In 2024 major record labels sued Suno and Udio over what?
questions.explanation: Labels sued Suno and Udio for training on copyrighted recordings without permission. Defamation is the tempting miss as another legal claim, but the suits were about copyright.

questions.text: Runway is best known for which generative capability?
questions.explanation: Runway is known for text-to-video and video editing tools. Speech synthesis is the tempting miss as the ElevenLabs niche.

questions.text: Pika is an AI startup focused on what?
questions.explanation: Pika builds AI video generation tools. Voice cloning is the tempting miss as the ElevenLabs space.

questions.text: ElevenLabs was founded by two engineers who previously worked on speech at which company?
questions.explanation: Founders Piotr Dabkowski and Mateusz Staniszewski both worked on speech at Google. Meta is the tempting miss as another big lab with speech research.

questions.text: HeyGen is best known for generating what kind of content?
questions.explanation: HeyGen creates photo-realistic AI avatar videos. Images is the tempting miss as the Midjourney and DALL-E space.

questions.text: Notion AI adds generative features to which type of product?
questions.explanation: Notion AI is built into Notion's note-taking and workspace app. Email client is the tempting miss as another productivity surface.

questions.text: Replika is best known as what kind of chatbot?
questions.explanation: Replika is an AI companion chatbot. A coding assistant is the tempting miss as the GitHub Copilot category.

questions.text: Replika was created by Eugenia Kuyda after the death of whom?
questions.explanation: Eugenia Kuyda built Replika from text messages after her friend Roman Mazurenko died. Her father is the tempting miss as another personal loss story.

questions.text: Snapchat's My AI is powered by which company's model?
questions.explanation: Snapchat's My AI runs on OpenAI's models. Google is the tempting miss as another major AI provider.

questions.text: Meta's AI assistant is built on which family of models?
questions.explanation: Meta AI is powered by Meta's Llama models. GPT is the tempting miss as the OpenAI family behind ChatGPT.

questions.text: Apple announced Apple Intelligence at which event in 2024?
questions.explanation: Apple Intelligence was announced at WWDC 2024. Google I/O is the tempting miss as Google's developer event.

questions.text: Apple Intelligence's optional ChatGPT integration is powered by which company's models?
questions.explanation: Apple Intelligence can hand complex requests to ChatGPT, powered by OpenAI. Google is the tempting miss because Apple later partnered with Google on Gemini.

questions.text: OpenAI's contested 2024 voice mode was named what?
questions.explanation: The voice at the center of the controversy was called Sky. Samantha is the tempting miss as the AI voice from the film Her, which OpenAI's demo evoked.

questions.text: DALL-E 2 was released by OpenAI in which year?
questions.explanation: DALL-E 2 arrived in 2022. 2021 is the tempting miss because that is when the original DALL-E was introduced.

questions.text: Midjourney was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: Midjourney was founded in 2021. 2022 is the tempting miss because that is when its open beta began.

questions.text: Claude was first released by Anthropic in which year?
questions.explanation: Claude launched in March 2023. 2024 is the tempting miss because that is when Claude 3 arrived.

questions.text: Google's Gemini model family was announced in which year?
questions.explanation: Gemini was announced in December 2023. 2024 is the tempting miss because that is when Bard was rebranded to Gemini.

questions.text: Microsoft began integrating Copilot into which operating system in 2023?
questions.explanation: Copilot was added to Windows 11 in late 2023. macOS is the tempting miss as another desktop OS, but Copilot's OS integration was Windows.

questions.text: Microsoft Copilot is integrated into which productivity suite?
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot brings AI into Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Google Workspace is the tempting miss as the competing suite.

questions.text: Perplexity AI was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: Perplexity AI was founded in August 2022. 2023 is the tempting miss because that is when its search engine launched to the public.

questions.text: Character.ai faced lawsuits in 2024 over what concern?
questions.explanation: Character.ai faced suits alleging its chatbots endangered teenagers. Copyright is the tempting miss as the other common AI legal issue.

questions.text: When Grok first launched in November 2023, access was limited to which users?
questions.explanation: Grok's early access was limited to paid X Premium subscribers. All X users is the tempting miss because Grok later opened up more broadly.

questions.text: NotebookLM's Audio Overviews feature mimics a podcast with how many AI hosts?
questions.explanation: Audio Overviews generate a conversation between two synthetic hosts. One is the tempting miss as a simpler format, but the viral feature was the two-host banter.

questions.text: The 2024 ChatGPT voice controversy involved which actor?
questions.explanation: Scarlett Johansson publicly objected that OpenAI's Sky voice sounded like hers. Emma Stone is the tempting miss as another well-known actress.

questions.text: Before its music generator, Suno released which open-source audio model in April 2023?
questions.explanation: Bark was Suno's open-source text-to-speech and audio model on GitHub, months before the music platform launched that December. VALL-E is the tempting miss because it was the other famous 2023 voice release, but it came from Microsoft, not Suno.

questions.text: In September 2024, Runway partnered with which film studio to build a custom video model on its catalog?
questions.explanation: The deal trained a custom model on the studio's catalog of over 20,000 film and television titles, reserved for Lionsgate-affiliated filmmakers. Universal is the tempting miss as the bigger studio name, but the first studio partnership of this kind was Lionsgate's.

questions.text: How do you accept a full Cursor Tab suggestion?
questions.explanation: Tab is Cursor's AI autocomplete: suggestions appear as grayed-out text and Tab accepts the full one, including multi-line and cross-file edits. Escape is the tempting miss because it is also part of the workflow, but it rejects the suggestion instead of accepting it.

questions.text: Which browser did Perplexity launch in July 2025?
questions.explanation: Comet is Perplexity's Chromium-based AI browser with the answer engine built in, first limited to top-tier subscribers and then free for everyone in October 2025. Arc is the tempting miss as the other startup browser people talk about, but it comes from The Browser Company, not Perplexity.

questions.text: The 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" described a model architecture that removed which component from earlier sequence to sequence systems?
questions.explanation: Eight Google authors dropped recurrence and convolution entirely and built the whole sequence model out of attention and feedforward layers. That is what made training parallel across the sequence, which is the property everything about scaling depends on.
